In-scope systems.value: Okta/Azure AD SSO and MFA, SailPoint IGA access certification, CyberArk privileged vaults, the payroll/benefits recordkeeping platform, the Workday HCM census interface and the participant self-service portal

Deadline reminders configured.value: SailPoint campaign auto-launches on the first business day of each quarter with reviewer reminders at day 10 and day 20 and manager escalation at day 25; Archer GRC tasks fire at T-60 and T-30 against the 31 March risk assessment date

checklist.step: Fix the ERISA plan data estate and freeze the system inventory
actions: Ask the Retirement Operations Administrator and the Benefits Administrator for the list of plans the company administers or acts as plan administrator for, with plan number, EIN and recordkeeping platform.
In the CMDB filter Configuration Items by Data Classification = 'Participant PII' and Business Service = retirement recordkeeping, group benefits or pension risk transfer.
Add every downstream store the query misses: reporting extracts in the enterprise data warehouse, SFTP landing zones for payroll contribution files, print/mail vendor drop folders and backup vaults.
Record for each system the owner, hosting model, data elements held (SSN, DOB, compensation, account balance, beneficiary) and whether participants access it directly.
Publish the inventory as the ERISA Plan Data Estate register and lock the version used for the quarter's testing.
checklist.done: every system holding or moving ERISA participant data is on a versioned register with a named owner and data elements listed.

checklist.step: Classify participant data elements and set the encryption standard per store
actions: Map each data element on the register to the classification scheme: SSN and bank account details as Restricted, balances and compensation as Confidential.
Set the required control per classification: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, tokenisation for SSN in analytics copies, and no participant data in non-production without masking.
Hand the per-system requirement to each system owner in writing with a target compliance date.
Record any store that cannot meet the standard as a named exception in the GRC platform with a compensating control.
checklist.done: each register entry carries a classification, a required encryption control and either a compliant status or a logged exception.

checklist.step: Enforce MFA on every workforce access path into the plan systems
actions: In Okta open Security > Authentication Policies and bind every application on the plan data register to the 'Plan Data - MFA Required' policy.
Set the policy factor constraints to phishing-resistant factors (FIDO2/WebAuthn or Okta Verify with number challenge) and deny SMS as a primary factor.
Hunt the bypass routes: legacy protocol endpoints, direct database logins, VPN-only paths and service accounts with interactive rights - list each and either front it with the IdP or vault it.
Export the Okta System Log filtered to the plan applications for the last 30 days and confirm every successful authentication carries a second factor event.
Send the residual non-MFA path list to the IT Security Manager with a remediation date.
checklist.done: every interactive path to a register system authenticates through the MFA policy, and any remaining path is listed with a dated remediation owner.

checklist.step: Enforce step-up authentication and anti-fraud controls on participant self-service
actions: Require MFA at participant registration and at every login to the participant portal, not only on high-risk actions.
Add step-up verification on the account-takeover targets: bank account change, address change, beneficiary change, loan request and distribution request.
Set a hold rule with the Retirement Operations Administrator so a distribution requested within 10 days of a bank or address change is queued for outbound voice verification.
Configure device and impossible-travel risk signals to force re-authentication and to raise an alert to the SOC.
Publish the participant-facing security guidance page describing MFA enrolment and reporting a suspected takeover.
checklist.done: participant login and every money-movement or beneficiary change requires a second factor, with a documented hold rule on post-change distributions.

checklist.step: Prove encryption at rest for every participant data store
actions: For each register system pull the storage configuration: TDE status for the recordkeeping database, storage account or EBS/disk encryption flags for hosts, bucket default encryption for object stores and backup catalogue encryption settings.
Record the algorithm and key length actually in force per store and compare it to the AES-256 requirement, not to what the vendor brochure claims.
Chase the exports that people forget: nightly participant extracts to the data warehouse, SFTP staging directories and print-vendor files - encrypt at rest or delete on transmit.
File the configuration exports as the encryption attestation for the quarter and raise a GRC exception for any store failing the standard.
checklist.done: every store on the register has a dated configuration export showing AES-256 at rest, or a logged exception with a remediation date.

checklist.step: Enforce TLS on every interface carrying participant data
actions: List every interface on the register: payroll contribution file feeds from ADP Payroll, the Workday HCM census interface, trustee and custodian files, print/mail vendor transfers and participant portal traffic.
Scan each endpoint and record the negotiated protocol and cipher suite; disable TLS 1.0/1.1 and anonymous or export ciphers at the load balancer.
Replace any plain FTP or unencrypted SMTP route with SFTP or PGP-encrypted payloads and get the counterpart's confirmation in writing.
Set certificate expiry monitoring so an expired certificate cannot force a fallback to an unencrypted path.
File the scan output per endpoint with the date and the interface owner.
checklist.done: every participant data interface is proven at TLS 1.2 or higher (or PGP-encrypted payload) by a dated scan, with certificate expiry monitored.

checklist.step: Vault and session-record privileged access to the recordkeeping platform
actions: Onboard every privileged credential for the recordkeeping platform, its database and its interface accounts into the CyberArk safe for ERISA plan systems.
Turn on password rotation on check-in and set the safe to require a ticket reference before a credential is released.
Enable session recording and keystroke logging for database administrator sessions touching participant tables.
Remove standing administrator rights and replace them with time-bound just-in-time elevation approved by the system owner.
Reconcile the safe contents to the register monthly and report unvaulted privileged accounts to the IT Security Manager.
checklist.done: no standing privileged credential to a plan system exists outside the vault, and administrator sessions are recorded.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly entitlement certification campaign
actions: In SailPoint create the campaign 'ERISA Plan Data - <quarter>' scoped to the applications on the plan data register plus their privileged entitlement groups.
Route line-item reviews to the entitlement owner rather than the line manager for privileged and segregation-sensitive entitlements.
Chase reviewers at day 10 and day 20; escalate anything open at day 25 to the reviewer's manager and to the IT Security Manager.
Confirm every 'revoke' decision is fulfilled by the provisioning connector and re-check the account 5 business days later - a revoke decision that never executed is worse than no campaign.
Export the campaign completion report with per-reviewer statistics and file it as the quarter's evidence.
checklist.done: the campaign is 100% complete, every revoke decision is confirmed executed, and the completion export is filed.

checklist.step: Close the joiner-mover-leaver loop against the HR system of record
actions: Take the daily termination and transfer feed from Workday HCM as the authoritative trigger; do not accept manager email as the sole trigger.
Match terminations to Okta and SailPoint accounts on employee id and compute hours-from-termination-to-disable for each.
Investigate every account still enabled beyond 24 hours, disable it the same day and record the cause (feed gap, contractor without an HR record, shared account).
Run a monthly orphan sweep for accounts with no matching active worker record and route each to the entitlement owner for deletion.
Report the deprovisioning timeliness statistic into the monthly control pack.
checklist.done: the termination feed reconciles to disabled accounts with a measured hours-to-disable figure and no unexplained orphan accounts.

checklist.step: Run the annual ERISA plan-data risk assessment
actions: Open the Risk Assessment record for the plan data estate and assess each of the 12 EBSA best practices against current control operation, citing the control ID and its most recent test result.

Rate threat scenarios that actually matter to a recordkeeper: participant account takeover leading to fraudulent distribution, mass extract of the census file, ransomware on the recordkeeping platform, and payroll file interception.
Score inherent and residual risk, name the treatment (accept, reduce, transfer) and give every reduce action an owner and a date.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer sign the assessment by 31 March and present it to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee.
Link the signed assessment to the compliance evidence repository record for the plan year.
checklist.done: a signed, dated risk assessment covering all 12 EBSA practices with owned treatment actions exists for the plan year.

checklist.step: Scan and patch the plan systems on the agreed SLA
actions: Tag every asset on the plan data register with the 'ERISA-PLAN' asset tag so it reports in its own dashboard.
Run authenticated scans weekly on those assets and confirm scan credentials actually authenticated - an unauthenticated scan is a false clean.
Drive remediation to the SLA: critical within 15 days, high within 30 days, and internet-facing critical within 7 days.
Open a ServiceNow change for each patch batch and record exceptions with a compensating control approved by the IT Security Manager.
Commission an annual third-party penetration test of the participant portal and the recordkeeping platform and track its findings to closure.
checklist.done: the ERISA-PLAN asset group shows authenticated scan coverage with no critical finding past SLA, and the annual pen test findings are tracked.

checklist.step: Monitor and alert on participant data access
actions: Confirm log sources from the recordkeeping platform, its database, Okta, CyberArk and the participant portal are all forwarding, and alarm on log source silence over 60 minutes.

Build detections for the recordkeeper-specific abuse cases: bulk participant record reads above a per-user daily threshold, off-hours census extract, repeated failed MFA followed by success, and bank detail change followed by distribution.
Set the triage path so a participant-data detection is worked at P2 or higher and pages the Incident Response Lead on confirmation.
Tune false positives monthly with the Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist so genuine batch jobs are allow-listed by service account, not by muting the rule.
Report detection coverage and mean time to triage into the monthly control pack.
checklist.done: all plan-system log sources are forwarding with participant-data detections live, tuned and routed to a named responder.

checklist.step: Prove business resiliency for the recordkeeping platform
actions: Set and document the RTO and RPO for the recordkeeping platform against the participant impact: contribution posting, distribution processing and portal availability.
Perform an actual restore of the participant database into an isolated environment at least annually and reconcile record counts and a sample of balances to the production statement date.
Confirm backups are immutable or air-gapped so a ransomware event cannot delete the recovery point.
Record the achieved recovery time against the RTO and raise a GRC action for any gap.
File the restore test report with the date, restore point, reconciliation result and sign-off.
checklist.done: a dated restore test report shows the participant database recovered within RTO with counts and balances reconciled.

checklist.step: Train the people who touch participant data
actions: Assign the annual ERISA participant data and fraud awareness module to every worker in the retirement operations, benefits and plan-servicing contact centre populations, taken from the Workday HCM org roster.
Cover the specific scenarios: caller impersonation on a distribution request, social engineering of a beneficiary change, and phishing that harvests portal credentials.
Run simulated phishing at least quarterly against the same population and enrol repeat clickers in remedial training.
Chase completion to 100% and report non-completers to their department head at day 30 past due.
Export the completion report and phishing results as evidence for the quarter.
checklist.done: 100% of the plan-servicing population has completed the annual module and quarterly phishing results are recorded.

checklist.step: Report control status to the plan fiduciary committee and retain the evidence
actions: Assemble the quarterly control pack: MFA and encryption coverage, certification completion, deprovisioning timeliness, vulnerability SLA, detection coverage and open exceptions with dates.
Map every metric back to the EBSA best practice it evidences so the pack reads as a fiduciary prudence record, not an IT dashboard.
Present to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and record the minute reference and any committee direction.
File the pack, the underlying exports and the minute reference in the compliance evidence repository under a 6-year ERISA 107 retention label.
Confirm the repository index makes the record retrievable by plan number, control ID and quarter.
checklist.done: the quarterly pack is presented, minuted and filed under a 6-year retention label retrievable by plan number and control ID.

testing.step: Build the population of plan-data systems and entitled accounts
actions: Extract from the CMDB every Configuration Item tagged ERISA-PLAN with owner, environment and data classification as at quarter end.
Extract from SailPoint IGA every account and entitlement on those applications, including service accounts and privileged groups.
Independently sweep for systems the tag missed by querying the data warehouse catalogue for tables containing participant identifiers and by listing SFTP endpoints used by payroll and print vendors.
Record the population counts and the extraction timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the system and account population is extracted from source tooling with counts, timestamps and an independent completeness sweep documented.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Reconcile the account population to the Workday HCM active worker roster on employee id and list accounts with no matching active worker.
Reconcile the system population to the ERISA Plan Data Estate register and investigate every system in one list and not the other.
Agree total counts to the numbers reported in the quarterly control pack and explain any difference before sampling.
Treat any unexplained difference as a completeness exception rather than adjusting the population to match the report.
testing.done: system and account counts reconcile to the register, the HR roster and the reported control pack, with differences explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of privileged entitlements and 100% of systems classified Restricted.
Take 40 accounts at random from the remaining population using a recorded random seed, plus all 25 most recent terminations in the quarter.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn independently.
Note the rationale for the coverage of each control objective the sample supports.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn with the seed, population size and selection date recorded, covering all privileged entitlements.

testing.step: Re-perform the MFA enforcement test in the identity platform
actions: In Okta open Security > Authentication Policies for each sampled application and read the bound policy and its factor constraints yourself before looking at the control owner's evidence.
Pull the System Log for the quarter filtered to those applications and search for successful authentications with no second factor event.
Attempt an authentication against one sampled non-production-equivalent path to confirm the policy actually blocks a single-factor login.
Screenshot the policy screen and the log query into the workpaper and record any single-factor success as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled application has an independently read policy, a log query showing no single-factor success, and a captured screen.

testing.step: Re-perform the encryption verification on sampled stores
actions: For each sampled store pull the live encryption configuration yourself (TDE status, disk or storage encryption flag, bucket default encryption) rather than accepting the attestation export.
Check the key length and the key rotation date and compare against the AES-256 and annual rotation requirement.
Scan one sampled interface endpoint and record the negotiated TLS version and cipher suite.
Record any store showing plaintext or a stale key as a fail, and note whether it was already on the exception register.
testing.done: sampled stores are independently confirmed at AES-256 with in-date keys, and every failure is recorded with its register status.

testing.step: Test the quality of the entitlement certification, not just its completion
actions: Pull the campaign decision export and compute the approve rate per reviewer and the median seconds between decisions.
Flag reviewers who approved 100% of line items in under 5 seconds each as probable rubber-stamping and re-test 5 of their approvals against actual job need.
For 20 sampled 'revoke' decisions confirm the entitlement is genuinely gone in the target application today.
Confirm privileged entitlements were reviewed by the entitlement owner and not self-certified by the account holder.
testing.done: certification quality is measured, rubber-stamp reviewers are re-tested, and every sampled revoke is confirmed executed in the target system.

testing.step: Recompute the deprovisioning timeliness maths
actions: For every sampled termination compute hours between the Workday termination effective timestamp and the Okta account disable timestamp.
Compare each to the 24-hour standard and list every breach with the elapsed hours.
For any account disabled late, query the SIEM for authentication activity in the gap window and treat any successful login after termination as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
Recompute the timeliness statistic reported in the control pack and reconcile to your own figure.
testing.done: hours-to-disable is recomputed per termination, breaches are listed, and any post-termination login is escalated as a breach.

testing.step: Trace the risk assessment to the 12 EBSA practices and to real control evidence
actions: Open the signed plan-data risk assessment and check each of the 12 EBSA best practices has an assessed control ID and a cited test result, not a narrative assertion.
For 6 practices trace the cited evidence to the underlying artefact (scan report, restore test, campaign export, pen test summary) and confirm the date falls inside the assessment period.
Confirm the CISO signature and date, and that the assessment was signed by 31 March and minuted at the plan committee.
Record any practice with no evidence or a stale artefact as a gap with the practice number named.
testing.done: all 12 EBSA practices trace to dated evidence, the assessment is signed by the deadline, and gaps are named by practice number.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception recording the system, account or practice affected, the control ID and the fiduciary impact on participant data.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (feed gap, policy not bound, unvaulted credential, stale key, reviewer rubber-stamp, missing evidence) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date proportional to risk and open a fiduciary breach assessment with Legal Counsel for any unauthorised access to participant data.
Carry every open issue into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with a root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute coverage percentages for MFA and encryption and the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the workpaper references behind each control objective.
Have the independent reviewer - who holds no administrative entitlement in the identity tooling - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open breaches to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage percentages, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

In-scope systems.value: Splunk SIEM detections and SOAR playbooks, CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint containment, the ITSM incident record, the recordkeeping platform and the participant self-service portal

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and General Counsel; re-approved annually after the exercise and re-issued whenever the notification matrix or a plan sponsor contract clause changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual tabletop completed by 30 September; plan sponsor notification inside the contractual window (typically 24 to 72 hours of determination); state breach notices on the shortest applicable statutory clock; disability claim decisions still due within 45 days of receipt under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(3) despite the outage

Deadline reminders configured.value: On incident declaration the SOAR playbook stamps the determination time and opens countdown tasks at 24, 48 and 72 hours; the annual exercise carries GRC reminders at T-90 and T-30 to the 30 September date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exercise scenario, participant list, injects, observations, after-action report and every incident record with its notification proofs retained 6 years under ERISA 107

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed exercise, unclosed after-action action, late notification or an incident worked without a declaration record is raised as a compliance exception with owner and due date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The IR Lead signs closure of every after-action action and the CISO signs off any notification decision taken not to notify

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The annual exercise record plus every security and availability incident in the year touching plan or participant data, taken from the ITSM incident queue and the SIEM case list

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Incident chronology with declaration and determination timestamps, forensic scope, affected participant counts by plan, notification letters and mailing proofs, assembled for an EBSA or state AG inquiry within 5 business days

checklist.step: Maintain the ERISA plan incident response plan as a standalone annex
actions: Write the plan annex specific to plan data rather than relying on the enterprise IR plan: named plans, recordkeeping platform, participant counts and the fiduciary duty owed under ERISA 404.

List the response team by role with 24x7 contact details: IR Lead, SOC Lead, forensics, Privacy Counsel, Retirement Operations Administrator, Communications Specialist and the plan sponsor relationship owner.
Set decision rights: who declares, who authorises containment that takes the participant portal offline, and who authorises notification.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer and General Counsel approve the annex and store the approved version in the compliance evidence repository with a printable offline copy.
checklist.done: an approved, dated plan annex names the plans, the response roles with contacts and the declaration and notification decision rights.

checklist.step: Define the severity matrix and the plan-data trigger
actions: Write the severity matrix so that any confirmed unauthorised access to participant PII or any recordkeeping outage over 4 hours is automatically P1, with no analyst discretion to downgrade.
Define the declaration event and require the SOAR playbook to stamp a declaration timestamp and a separate determination-of-breach timestamp - the notification clocks run from the second one.
Set the containment authority thresholds, including who may suspend distributions or portal logins during a suspected takeover campaign.
Publish the matrix to the SOC and confirm the triage queue routes plan-data alerts to it.
checklist.done: the matrix forces P1 on participant data exposure and the playbook stamps separate declaration and determination timestamps.

checklist.step: Build the notification matrix by recipient and legal clock
actions: Pull the plan sponsor service agreements from the contract repository and record each contract's breach notification window (commonly 24, 48 or 72 hours of determination) against the plan name.
Record the state breach notification requirement for each state of participant residence, including the shortest clock and any attorney general and consumer reporting agency thresholds.
Record the DOL/EBSA and, where the plan is also HIPAA-covered, the HHS Office for Civil Rights routes, with the 60-day individual notice and annual small-breach log rules for health plan data.
Name the approver for each notification type and the template letter to be used.
Refresh the matrix annually and whenever a plan sponsor contract is renewed.
checklist.done: every plan has a recorded notification window per recipient with the shortest applicable clock, an approver and a template letter.

checklist.step: Scope and schedule the annual exercise
actions: Set the exercise date before 30 September and book the participants by name: IR Lead, SOC Lead, forensics, Privacy Counsel, Retirement Operations Administrator, Benefits Administrator, Communications Specialist and a plan sponsor relationship owner.

Choose a scenario grounded in recordkeeper risk - for example credential stuffing against the participant portal followed by fraudulent distribution requests, or ransomware on the recordkeeping database during contribution processing.
State the objectives to be evidenced: declaration timing, participant scoping, notification decision, portal containment and continuity of benefit claim decisions.
Circulate the invitation with the objectives but not the injects, and appoint an observer to time each decision.
checklist.done: a dated exercise is scheduled before 30 September with named cross-functional participants and written objectives.

checklist.step: Run the annual tabletop exercise
actions: Run the scenario in timed injects: initial SIEM alert, confirmation of unauthorised access, discovery that the census extract was copied, then a plan sponsor phone call demanding facts.
Force the team to produce the artefacts live: the declaration record in ITSM, an affected-participant count by plan, a draft sponsor notification and a decision on portal suspension.
Have the observer record the wall-clock time of each decision against the contractual notification window.
Inject the operational consequence: with the claims system down, confirm the team states how the 45-day disability decision deadline under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(3) will still be met.
Close with a hot wash capturing what did not work while it is still fresh.
checklist.done: the exercise is run with timed injects, live artefacts produced and each decision time recorded by an observer.

checklist.step: Validate detection and containment technically, not only on paper
actions: Run controlled tests of the plan-data detections: simulate a bulk participant record read, an off-hours census extract and a bank-detail change followed by a distribution request.
Confirm each fires an alert, reaches the SOC queue at the intended severity, and record the time from action to alert.
Test containment on a non-production equivalent: isolate a host in CrowdStrike Falcon and disable a portal session in the identity platform, timing both.
Raise a detection engineering ticket for every test that produced no alert or a wrong severity.
checklist.done: each simulated plan-data abuse case produced a timed alert at the right severity, and every miss has a detection ticket.

checklist.step: Write the after-action report and drive the actions to closure
actions: Write up the exercise: scenario, participants, timeline of decisions, objectives met and not met, and the artefacts produced.
Convert every observation into a GRC action with a named owner and a due date inside 90 days.
Update the IR annex, the severity matrix and the notification matrix for anything the exercise proved wrong.
Report the report and the open actions to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and record the minute reference.
Track the actions weekly until closed and refuse to close on 'discussed' - require the changed artefact.
checklist.done: a dated after-action report exists with every observation converted into an owned, dated GRC action and the annex updated.

checklist.step: Run 24x7 detection and triage intake for plan systems
actions: Confirm the plan-data detections carry the ERISA-PLAN tag so the triage queue routes them to the elevated playbook.
Require the analyst to open an ITSM incident with the plan name and the suspected record count within 30 minutes of triage.
Escalate to the Incident Response Lead on confirmation of any unauthorised access to participant data, day or night.
Report weekly on plan-data alert volume, mean time to triage and any alert closed without a documented rationale.
checklist.done: plan-data alerts route to the elevated playbook with an ITSM incident opened inside 30 minutes and escalation to the IR Lead on confirmation.

checklist.step: On declaration, run forensics and scope the affected participants
actions: Preserve volatile evidence and take forensic images before remediation, and log the chain of custody with times and handlers.
Establish the access window from authentication and database audit logs, then pull the exact rows or files touched.
Convert the technical scope into a participant list with the Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist: participant id, plan number, plan name, state of residence and the data elements exposed.
State explicitly whether SSN, bank details or health information were in scope - these drive the notification clocks and content.
Deliver the scoped list and the chronology to Privacy Counsel and stamp the determination time.
checklist.done: a chain-of-custody forensic record and a per-plan, per-state affected participant list with data elements exposed is delivered and time-stamped.

checklist.step: Compute the notification clocks and record the decision
actions: Take the determination timestamp and compute the due date for each recipient from the notification matrix: plan sponsor contractual window, each state's statutory clock by participant residence, and any health-plan 60-day individual notice.
Identify the single shortest clock and set that as the working deadline for the whole response.
Where a decision is made not to notify, write the reasoned basis (for example encryption safe harbour with keys demonstrably uncompromised) and have the Chief Info Security Officer countersign it.
Record every due date and its owner on the incident record so the countdown is visible to the response team.
checklist.done: each recipient has a computed due date from the determination timestamp, with the shortest clock identified and any no-notify decision countersigned.

checklist.step: Notify the plan sponsor and co-fiduciaries inside the contractual window
actions: Draft the sponsor notification from the template: what happened, when it was determined, plans and participant counts affected, data elements, containment taken and next steps.
Have Legal Counsel clear the wording before it is sent - no speculation on cause or count.
Send through the contractually named contact and channel and capture the delivery receipt and time on the incident record.
Offer the sponsor a briefing call within 24 hours and record who attended and what was committed.
checklist.done: each affected plan sponsor is notified inside its contractual window with a cleared letter and a captured delivery timestamp.

checklist.step: Notify affected participants and regulators on the applicable clocks
actions: Produce the participant notice covering the incident description, data elements, date range, steps taken, credit monitoring offer and a dedicated phone line.
Run the mailing against the current address file from the recordkeeping platform, handle returned mail with a skip trace, and record counts sent, delivered and returned.
File the state attorney general notices and consumer reporting agency notices where thresholds are exceeded, on the shortest clock.
Brief the contact centre with a scripted response and an escalation path before the notices land, not after.
File copies of every notice, the recipient list and the submission confirmations on the incident record.
checklist.done: participant and regulator notices are sent within the computed deadlines with counts, copies and submission confirmations filed.

checklist.step: Protect benefit claim service levels while the incident is open
actions: List every claim with a statutory decision deadline falling inside the outage window, with its receipt date and its 45-day decision date under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(3).
Work the at-risk claims on the documented manual workaround and record each decision and its date outside the system.
Where an extension is genuinely required, issue the written extension notice to the claimant before the original deadline expires, stating the reason and the expected decision date.
Reconcile the manual decisions back into the claims system when service is restored and confirm no deadline was silently missed.
checklist.done: every claim with a deadline inside the outage has a recorded decision or a timely written extension notice, reconciled back on restoration.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and change the controls
actions: Hold the post-incident review within 15 business days of closure with the responders and the Retirement Operations Administrator.
Establish the root cause and the control that should have prevented or detected it, naming the control ID.
Raise dated remediation actions and feed the scenario into the next annual exercise and into the SOC detection backlog.
Report the incident, cost and remediation plan to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee as a fiduciary matter and minute it.
checklist.done: a post-incident review inside 15 business days names a root cause, a control ID and dated remediation, reported to the plan committee.

checklist.step: Retain the exercise and incident records for the retention period
actions: File the exercise pack (scenario, invitation, injects, observer notes, after-action report) and each incident record with its chronology, forensic report, participant list and notification proofs.
Apply the 6-year ERISA 107 retention label and place a legal hold on any incident with litigation or regulator interest.
Confirm the repository index makes the records retrievable by plan number, incident id and calendar year.
Run an annual completeness check that every ITSM incident tagged ERISA-PLAN has a matching repository record.
checklist.done: exercise and incident records are filed under a 6-year retention label, retrievable by plan number and incident id, with holds applied where needed.

testing.step: Build the population of exercises and plan-data incidents for the year
actions: Extract every incident with the ERISA-PLAN tag, severity P1 or P2, or a plan name in the affected service field, for the period under test.
Extract the SIEM case list for the same period and the exercise record from the GRC platform.
Add availability incidents on the recordkeeping platform and participant portal so outage events cannot hide among security tickets.
Record the population counts, the extract queries and the timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the incident and exercise population is extracted from ITSM, the SIEM and GRC with queries, counts and timestamps recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Reconcile the ITSM extract to the SOC weekly reporting totals and to the SIEM case list and investigate every case with no incident ticket.
Reconcile plan sponsor breach notifications sent (from the sponsor correspondence log) back to declared incidents - a notification with no incident record is a control failure.
Agree the exercise count to the annual control pack and confirm the exercise date falls before 30 September.
Explain every difference in writing before sampling rather than adjusting the population.
testing.done: incident counts reconcile across ITSM, the SIEM and sponsor correspondence, with all differences explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of P1 incidents, 100% of incidents where any notification was sent, and 100% of exercises.
Take 15 further incidents at random from the remainder using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note which control objective each sampled item is intended to evidence.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all P1 and notifying incidents plus the exercise is drawn with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the exercise evidence review
actions: Open the exercise record and confirm the scenario, attendee list, injects and observer timing sheet exist as artefacts, not as a calendar entry.
Check the attendee list actually includes plan operations, legal and communications roles - a security-only exercise does not evidence the fiduciary duty.
Confirm the live artefacts (declaration record, participant count, draft sponsor letter, portal containment decision) were produced during the exercise.
Trace 5 after-action observations to GRC actions and check their status and due dates today.
testing.done: the exercise is evidenced by scenario, attendees, injects, timing and live artefacts, with after-action actions traced to current GRC status.

testing.step: Re-perform the severity and declaration judgement on sampled incidents
actions: Read the incident facts and reach your own severity conclusion against the published matrix before reading the assigned severity.
Confirm the declaration timestamp and the separate determination-of-breach timestamp are both recorded and are supported by the underlying log or forensic finding.
Flag any participant-data incident held below P1, any downgrade with no documented rationale, and any incident where the determination timestamp was set after the notification was already sent.
Capture the incident record screen into the workpaper for each sampled item.
testing.done: each sampled incident carries an independent severity re-performance with both timestamps verified against underlying evidence.

testing.step: Trace the forensic scope to the participant list and its identifiers
actions: For each notifying incident take the forensic access window and independently query the affected table or file access log for the same window.
Reconcile your record count to the affected participant list count and investigate any difference greater than zero.
Confirm the participant list carries plan number, participant id, state of residence and data elements exposed - a headline count with no identifiers cannot support a notification.
Confirm chain of custody entries exist for every forensic image with handler and time.
testing.done: forensic scope is independently recomputed and agrees to the participant list, which carries plan, participant and state identifiers.

testing.step: Recompute every notification deadline and compare to the actual send
actions: For each notifying incident recompute the plan sponsor due date as determination timestamp plus the contractual window taken from the service agreement itself, not from the matrix.
Recompute each state statutory due date from the participant residence list and identify the shortest clock.
Compare each computed due date to the actual send timestamp on the correspondence record and record the variance in hours.
Treat any send after the due date as a reportable breach and any 'no notification' decision without a countersigned rationale as a fail.
testing.done: every notification deadline is recomputed from the underlying contract and statute and compared to the actual send, with variances in hours recorded.

testing.step: Test that benefit claim deadlines survived the outage
actions: For each availability incident affecting claims, extract the disability and life claims with a decision deadline inside the outage window.
Recompute the 45-day decision date from the claim receipt date under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(3) for each.
Confirm each claim shows either a decision on or before that date or a written extension notice issued before the original deadline expired.
Log any silent miss as a regulatory breach and refer it to Employment Counsel.
testing.done: every claim with a deadline inside an outage is proven decided in time or covered by a timely written extension notice.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the incident id, the failed step (declaration, scoping, notification, claim deadline) and the fiduciary impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (matrix out of date, determination timestamp missing, contact list stale, detection gap, workaround untested) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and open a fiduciary breach assessment with General Counsel for any late statutory notification.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the late-notification count and the proportion of P1 incidents with complete declaration, scoping and notification evidence.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the incident ids and workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer - who took no part in the exercise or in any sampled response - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late notification to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, late-notification count and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Signs the annual written certification that the ERISA plan data security programme operated for the plan year, and co-signs the ERISA 103(a)(3)(C) certification of investment information the company issues as a regulated insurance carrier

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - ERISA 104(a) and 29 CFR 2520.104a-5 for the annual report, 29 CFR 2520.103-5 and 2520.103-8 for the carrier certification supporting a 103(a)(3)(C) limited-scope audit, read with the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices and Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01

In-scope processes.value: Annual attestation over the plan data security programme and over the investment information the company certifies to plan administrators of the retirement, group annuity and pension risk transfer contracts it holds as insurer or recordkeeper

In-scope systems.value: Control evidence assembled from Archer GRC, SailPoint IGA, Splunk SIEM and Qualys, plus the separate account and general account valuations from the ERP general ledger, signed through DocuSign and filed in the evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Plan Data Certification Procedure: control inventory to be certified, evidence collection calendar, sub-certification from each control owner, gap and qualification handling, legal review and officer signature

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and Head of Compliance; the certification wording itself is approved by Legal Counsel each year before signature

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Evidence cut-off at 31 December plan year end; sub-certifications in by 15 January; carrier 103(a)(3)(C) certification issued to plan administrators by 31 January so the plan auditor can work to the 31 July Form 5500 date; signed programme certification filed by 28 February

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC tasks issue to each control owner on 2 January with reminders at 8 and 12 January; a 31 January hard-stop task on the carrier certification with escalation to the Controller if any plan is unissued

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed certification, every sub-certification, the control evidence index and the certified investment schedules retained 6 years under ERISA 107 and available to the plan's independent qualified public accountant

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any control that cannot be sub-certified, any qualification carried into the certification, and any plan whose carrier certification is issued late is logged with owner, disposition and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off the disposition of every qualification and confirms remediation before the following year's certification is signed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The signed certification and every underlying sub-certification for the plan year, plus every plan and contract for which a 103(a)(3)(C) carrier certification was required and the schedules certified in each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unsupported assertions - any certified control with no dated evidence is a fail; 100% of required carrier certifications issued by 31 January; any certification signed while a known material control gap is undisclosed is an outright fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per plan year immediately after signature, with a mid-year readiness check in July on evidence completeness

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The reviewer must not own any certified control and must not have provided a sub-certification for the year under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual certification test workpaper (sub-certification inventory, evidence trace, valuation reconciliation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Certification / <plan year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed certification, control evidence index, certified investment schedules with the carrier officer signature, and the issuance log by plan, producible for an EBSA investigation or a plan auditor request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance responds to EBSA and to plan auditors; the Controller owns questions on certified values; Legal Counsel clears any statement qualifying or withdrawing a previously issued certification

checklist.step: Confirm what is being certified and on what legal basis
actions: Write the certification scope statement for the plan year: the plan data security programme, the plans covered by plan number and EIN, and the contracts for which the company must issue a 103(a)(3)(C) certification as insurance carrier.

Confirm with Legal Counsel the statutory basis for each certification - 29 CFR 2520.103-5 for carrier-held investment information and the fiduciary prudence record under ERISA 404 for the programme certification.
Ask the Retirement Operations Administrator for the list of plan administrators expecting a certification this year and any new contracts written during the year.
Circulate the scope statement to control owners and the Controller before evidence collection starts.
checklist.done: a dated scope statement names the certifications, the legal basis for each and every plan and contract in scope.

checklist.step: Map the control set to be certified to numbered control IDs
actions: List in Archer every control that the certification statement will assert operated, mapped to the 12 EBSA best practices and to the control owner.
For each control record the test method that will evidence it: tooling export, sample test result, third-party report or management sign-off.
Delete assertions from the draft statement that no control actually supports rather than manufacturing evidence for them.
Publish the control-to-assertion map so the signer can see the chain from sentence to evidence.
checklist.done: every sentence of the draft certification maps to a numbered control with an owner and a named evidence type.

checklist.step: Collect control operating evidence for the whole period
actions: Pull the four quarterly SailPoint certification exports, the monthly MFA and encryption coverage reports, the Qualys SLA reports, the annual restore test and the signed risk assessment.
Check the evidence covers the whole plan year and not just the fourth quarter - a certification on year-end evidence certifies one day.
Index each artefact against its control ID with the date, the producing system and the person who pulled it.
Chase gaps immediately and record any period with no evidence as a scope limitation rather than assuming the control operated.
checklist.done: each control has period-complete, dated evidence indexed to its control ID, with any evidence gap recorded as a scope limitation.

checklist.step: Obtain sub-certifications from each control owner
actions: Issue a sub-certification form to each control owner on 2 January stating the specific assertion they are signing and the evidence references behind it.
Require the owner to affirm, qualify or refuse - a qualified sub-certification must name the period, the affected systems and the compensating control.
Collect all sub-certifications by 15 January through DocuSign so signature identity and timestamp are captured.
Escalate any owner who has not signed by 15 January to their department head and to the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: every control owner has affirmed or qualified in a timestamped signed sub-certification by 15 January.

checklist.step: Obtain and review the service organisation reports behind the certification
actions: Collect the current SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports for the recordkeeping platform, the custodian and the print/mail vendor.
Check each report period covers the plan year and obtain a bridge letter for any gap between the report period end and 31 December.
Read the complementary user entity controls and confirm the company actually performs each one, naming the internal control ID that does so.
List every qualified opinion or exception in the reports and assess its effect on the certification with the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: period-covering SOC reports with bridge letters are on file, user entity controls are mapped to internal control IDs, and report exceptions are assessed.

checklist.step: Assemble the investment information to be certified to plan administrators
actions: For each plan holding a group annuity or separate account contract, produce the year-end schedule of assets held, income, gains and losses and expenses attributable to the contract.
Confirm the values are those held by the company as a regulated insurance carrier and that the certification will state so, as 29 CFR 2520.103-5 requires.
Reconcile unit values and units outstanding to the separate account records and to the participant balances in the recordkeeping platform.
Flag any asset the company does not hold or value itself - it cannot be covered by the certification and must be disclosed to the plan administrator.
checklist.done: each in-scope plan has a year-end investment schedule limited to carrier-held, carrier-valued assets and reconciled to unit records.

checklist.step: Reconcile the certified values to the general ledger and the statutory statement
actions: Tie the total separate account and general account balances on the certified schedules to the corresponding ledger accounts at 31 December.
Tie the same totals to the separate account exhibit in the statutory annual statement so the certification cannot disagree with the filed financials.
Investigate and clear every reconciling item over the agreed threshold and document the explanation on the reconciliation.
Have the Controller sign the reconciliation before the certification is drafted.
checklist.done: certified totals agree to the general ledger and the statutory separate account exhibit, on a reconciliation signed by the Controller.

checklist.step: Draft the certification statements
actions: Draft the programme certification stating the period, the plans covered, the assertions made, the evidence basis and any qualification, in the officer's own voice.
Draft the carrier certification for each plan in the wording 29 CFR 2520.103-5 requires - that the company certifies the completeness and accuracy of the information it holds and provides.
Do not certify beyond what the company holds and values; name the excluded assets explicitly in the letter.
Attach the schedule and the evidence index reference to each draft and circulate for review.
checklist.done: both certification drafts state period, scope, assertions, exclusions and qualifications, with schedules and evidence references attached.

checklist.step: Run a pre-signature gap review
actions: Take the draft certification and test 10 assertions back to their evidence without help from the control owner.
Check every open high-rated GRC exception is either remediated or disclosed as a qualification in the draft.
Confirm no sub-certification was refused or silently withdrawn after the draft was written.
Report the gap review conclusion in writing to the Chief Info Security Officer before signature - a certification signed over a known undisclosed gap is the failure mode this step exists to stop.
checklist.done: a written pre-signature gap review confirms tested assertions are supported and every open high exception is disclosed or remediated.

checklist.step: Record qualifications and their remediation plans
actions: Log each qualification as a GRC issue with the control ID, the period affected, the compensating control and the remediation owner.
Set remediation dates that land before the next certification cycle and put them on the control owner's objectives.
Link each qualification to the sentence in the certification that discloses it so the disclosure cannot drift from the issue.
Report the qualification list to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee with the certification.
checklist.done: every qualification is a tracked GRC issue with a compensating control, an owner and a remediation date before the next cycle.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review of the certification wording
actions: Review both drafts for statements that exceed what the evidence supports or that assume fiduciary status the company does not hold.
Confirm the carrier certification language matches 29 CFR 2520.103-5 and does not accidentally certify assets held by a third-party custodian.
Confirm the officer signing has the authority to bind the company for the certification given.
Return the cleared drafts with any required wording changes marked and dated.
checklist.done: both certifications are legally cleared in writing, with wording confined to what the evidence and the company's role support.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer signature
actions: Read the evidence index and the pre-signature gap review before signing, not the summary slide.
Sign the programme certification through DocuSign so the signature identity, date and document hash are captured.
Route the carrier certifications for signature by the authorised officer named in the legal review, with the same capture.
Refuse signature and send back any certification whose qualifications do not match the open GRC issue list.
checklist.done: certifications carry an authorised officer's timestamped electronic signature, with qualifications matching the open issue list.

checklist.step: Issue the carrier certification to each plan administrator by 31 January
actions: Send each plan administrator the signed certification with its investment schedule through the contractual contact and channel.
Meet the 31 January target so the plan's independent qualified public accountant can complete the 103(a)(3)(C) limited-scope work in time for the 31 July Form 5500 deadline.
Capture the delivery date and recipient on the issuance log, one row per plan number.
Chase any plan with no confirmed delivery by 5 February and escalate to the Controller.
checklist.done: every in-scope plan administrator has a delivered, signed certification with its schedule, logged by plan number and date.

checklist.step: Feed the certification into the Form 5500 and plan audit workstream
actions: Hand the certified schedules to the Form 5500 preparer for Schedule A and Schedule H line items and note the certification reference on the preparation file.
Answer the plan auditor's requests for the certification and its supporting reconciliation through a single named contact to keep versions controlled.
Where the auditor challenges a certified value, route the query to the Controller and record the resolution against the plan number.
Confirm the plan's Form 5500 audit report reflects the limited-scope certification where relied upon.
checklist.done: certified schedules are handed to the 5500 preparer and the plan auditor with a single contact and a recorded resolution for every challenge.

checklist.step: Retain the signed certifications and their evidence
actions: File the signed programme certification, every sub-certification, the evidence index, the SOC reports and bridge letters, the reconciliations and every issued carrier certification with its schedule.
Apply the 6-year ERISA 107 retention label and index by plan number, plan year and certification type.
Confirm the issuance log is filed alongside so late or missing issuances are visible years later.
Run a completeness check that the number of filed carrier certifications equals the number of in-scope plans.
checklist.done: all certifications and their supporting evidence are filed under a 6-year retention label, with filed count equal to the in-scope plan count.

testing.step: Build the population of certifications required and issued
actions: Extract from the contract system every plan and group annuity or separate account contract in force at 31 December for which a carrier certification is required.
Extract the issuance log and the filed certification set from the compliance evidence repository.
Extract the sub-certification list from DocuSign with signer, date and document status.
Record the three population counts, the extraction method and the timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: required-certification, issued-certification and sub-certification populations are extracted with counts, method and timestamps recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the populations to the source of record
actions: Reconcile required certifications to issued certifications by plan number and list every plan with no issued certification.
Reconcile the sub-certification list to the control-to-assertion map and list every certified control with no signed sub-certification.
Reconcile new contracts written during the year to the required list so a mid-year plan cannot fall out of scope.
Explain every difference in writing before sampling.
testing.done: every required certification and every certified control reconciles to an issued document or an explained, written difference.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of qualified sub-certifications and 100% of plans whose certification was issued after 31 January.
Take 20 plans at random from the remaining issued population using a recorded seed, plus 12 certified assertions at random.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
State which assertion each sampled item tests.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all qualifications and all late issuances is drawn with the seed and dates recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the assertion-to-evidence trace
actions: For each sampled assertion open the cited evidence artefact and confirm it exists, is dated inside the plan year and actually supports the words used.
Check period completeness - a quarterly control needs four exports, not one.
Reject evidence that is a summary of evidence: require the source system export with its generation timestamp.
Record every assertion with missing, stale or partial evidence as an exception naming the control ID.
testing.done: each sampled assertion traces to period-complete source-system evidence, or is recorded as an exception by control ID.

testing.step: Re-perform the valuation reconciliation on sampled plans
actions: For each sampled plan take the certified schedule totals and independently agree them to the ledger account balance at 31 December.
Agree units outstanding and unit value to the separate account records and recompute the extended value.
Agree the total to the statutory annual statement separate account exhibit.
Record any difference in amount and percentage and treat an uncleared difference as a fail, not a rounding note.
testing.done: sampled certified totals are independently agreed to the ledger, the unit records and the statutory exhibit, with differences quantified.

testing.step: Test the sub-certification chain for authority and honesty
actions: Confirm each sampled sub-certification was signed by the recorded control owner and not by a delegate without written authority.
Compare the sub-certification signature date to the evidence cut-off and to the 15 January deadline and record late signatures.
For each qualified sub-certification confirm the qualification is disclosed in the signed certification wording.
Search the GRC exception list for high-rated open issues at signature date and confirm each was disclosed - an undisclosed known gap is the headline exception.
testing.done: sub-certifications are signed by authorised owners on time, and every qualification and open high exception is traced into the certification wording.

testing.step: Recompute the issuance deadline maths
actions: For each sampled plan compute days from 31 December plan year end to the logged issuance date.
Compare each to the 31 January internal target and to the plan's own audit timetable where the administrator supplied one.
Assess whether any late issuance put the plan's 31 July Form 5500 date or its extended 15 October date at risk and record the assessment.
List every late issuance with the elapsed days and the plan number.
testing.done: issuance elapsed days are recomputed per plan, late issuances are listed, and their effect on the Form 5500 timetable is assessed.

testing.step: Test the service organisation report coverage behind the certification
actions: Open each SOC report relied on and confirm the report period plus bridge letter covers 1 January to 31 December.
Confirm each complementary user entity control is mapped to an internal control that was itself evidenced for the year.
Read the exceptions section and check each exception was assessed in writing for its effect on the certification.
Record any reliance on an out-of-period or qualified report as an exception.
testing.done: every relied-on SOC report covers the full year with mapped user entity controls and written assessment of its exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan number or control ID, the failed element and the effect on the certification's reliability.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (evidence not retained, control not operated, valuation break, late issuance, undisclosed gap, unauthorised signer) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next certification cycle and, where a certification was issued on unsupported information, open a withdrawal or re-issue assessment with Legal Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's readiness check as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner and remediation date, with a re-issue assessment opened where the certification was unsupported.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the proportion of assertions supported by period-complete evidence and the count of certifications issued after 31 January.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the plan numbers and workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer - who owns no certified control and gave no sub-certification - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unsupported certification to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and the Audit Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with support percentages, a stated conclusion and committee reporting dates is filed in the evidence repository.

In-scope processes.value: Selection, contracting, annual assessment and offboarding of covered service providers to the ERISA plans: recordkeepers, custodians and trustees, investment managers, TPAs, print and mail vendors, participant contact centre outsourcers and cloud hosting for plan data
