Compliance procedure documented.value: Plan Service Provider Oversight Procedure: covered-provider determination, pre-contract cyber and financial due diligence, 408(b)(2) disclosure capture before the contract is entered, tiering by participant data access, annual reassessment and exit data-return

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Info Security Officer; reviewed annually and re-approved whenever the plan committee changes the provider tiering or delegation thresholds

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: 408(b)(2) disclosure received before the contract is entered or renewed; provider change disclosures inside 60 days of the provider learning of the change; fiduciary information requests answered inside 30 days; Tier 1 reassessment annually on the contract anniversary

Deadline reminders configured.value: Icertis obligation alerts at T-120, T-90 and T-30 to each contract anniversary; a 45-day amber and 60-day red clock on every logged provider change; a 20-day amber on any open fiduciary information request

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Due diligence packs, 408(b)(2) disclosures, SOC 2 Type II reports and bridge letters, questionnaires, penetration test summaries, benchmarking and the reasonableness determination retained 6 years under ERISA 107 from contract termination

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing or late 408(b)(2) disclosure, expired SOC report, unremediated critical finding, missing breach notification clause or overdue reassessment is logged as a vendor exception with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off continued use of any provider carrying an open critical finding and signs every decision to contract without a complete 408(b)(2) disclosure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All covered service providers to the ERISA plans active at any point in the year, plus every new engagement, renewal and termination in the period, taken from the vendor master and the contract repository

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero Tier 1 providers without a current SOC 2 Type II covering the year; zero contracts entered or renewed without a 408(b)(2) disclosure on file dated before execution; any fiduciary information request answered after 30 days is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per vendor and annual; the test runs annually over the full provider population with a quarterly interim test over new engagements and renewals in that quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The reviewer must not have performed any sampled assessment nor hold commercial ownership of any sampled provider relationship

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual plan service provider oversight test workpaper (provider population, disclosure trace, assessment re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Vendor Oversight / <plan year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Provider register with tiering, the 408(b)(2) disclosure file per provider, assessment reports, benchmarking and the fiduciary reasonableness determination, producible for an EBSA investigation within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the EBSA response on provider oversight; Legal Counsel handles any prohibited transaction exposure arising from a failed 408(b)(2) disclosure, including the class exemption relief route under 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1)(ix)

checklist.step: Build the covered service provider register
actions: Extract from the vendor master every supplier with spend charged to a plan or paid from plan assets, and every supplier flagged as receiving participant data.
Add the providers procurement never sees: sub-custodians named in the custody agreement, print and mail subcontractors, and cloud regions hosting the recordkeeping platform.

For each entry record the services provided, whether the provider expects 1,000 dollars or more in direct or indirect compensation, and whether it is a fiduciary or registered investment adviser to the plan.
Apply the covered-service-provider determination and record the reasoning per provider, not per category.
Publish the register and reconcile it to the contract repository so no provider exists in one and not the other.
checklist.done: a published register lists every covered service provider with services, compensation basis, fiduciary status and a recorded determination.

checklist.step: Tier the providers by participant data access and fiduciary role
actions: Set Tier 1 for providers holding participant PII or plan assets or exercising discretion, Tier 2 for those with limited data and no discretion, Tier 3 for no data access.
Record the data elements each provider receives - SSN, DOB, compensation, balances, bank details, health information - taken from the actual interface specification, not the contract recital.
Set the assessment depth per tier: Tier 1 annual SOC 2 Type II plus questionnaire plus evidence review, Tier 2 annual questionnaire, Tier 3 attestation only.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer approve the tiering and record it against each register entry.
checklist.done: every provider carries an approved tier based on actual data elements received and discretion held, with the assessment depth set.

checklist.step: Run pre-contract cyber and operational due diligence
actions: Request the SOC 2 Type II report, the most recent penetration test summary, the information security policy and the incident history for the last 24 months.

Assess against the EBSA best practices the provider is expected to meet: access controls and MFA, encryption, secure SDLC, third-party assessment of its own subcontractors, incident response and business resiliency with stated RTO and RPO.
Confirm where participant data will be stored and processed, including offshore locations and subcontractors, and record it.
Score the provider and write a recommendation with named conditions; issue findings the provider must close before go-live.
File the due diligence pack against the register entry.
checklist.done: a scored, dated due diligence pack with named pre-go-live conditions exists before any participant data is shared.

checklist.step: Obtain the 408(b)(2) disclosure before the contract is entered
actions: Request the written disclosure covering the services to be provided, the provider's status as fiduciary or registered investment adviser, and all direct and indirect compensation with the payer, payee and formula.

Check the disclosure describes compensation among related parties and any termination compensation, and that recordkeeping compensation is disclosed even where it is bundled or offset by revenue sharing.
Refuse to execute until the disclosure is on file dated before signature - a contract entered without it is a prohibited transaction, not a paperwork gap.
Where a disclosure error is later found, invoke the good-faith correction route and disclose the correct information within 30 days of learning of it.
File the disclosure in Icertis against the contract with the receipt date recorded.
checklist.done: a dated 408(b)(2) disclosure covering services, fiduciary status and all direct and indirect compensation is on file before contract execution.

checklist.step: Negotiate the security, audit and breach clauses into the contract
actions: Require the clause set: encryption to the company standard, MFA on all access to plan data, annual SOC 2 Type II delivery, right to audit or to receive assessment evidence, and subcontractor flow-down and approval.
Set a breach notification clause with a hard clock - notification to the company within 24 hours of the provider determining an incident affecting plan data.
Require cyber liability and fidelity bond coverage at named limits with the company as additional insured or loss payee where appropriate.
Require data return and certified destruction on termination within a stated number of days and prohibit use of participant data for the provider's own purposes.
Record each clause as a tracked obligation in Icertis with its owner and review date rather than leaving it in the PDF.
checklist.done: the executed contract carries the encryption, MFA, SOC delivery, audit, 24-hour breach, insurance and data-return clauses, each tracked as an obligation.

checklist.step: Verify insurance, bonding and financial standing
actions: Collect the certificate of insurance for cyber liability, professional liability and the ERISA fidelity bond, and check limits, retentions and expiry dates against the contract.
Confirm the ERISA 412 bonding requirement is met for any provider handling plan funds, at 10 percent of funds handled subject to the statutory cap.
Review the provider's audited financial statements or credit report for going-concern risk and record the assessment.
Set renewal reminders 30 days before each certificate expiry and chase replacements.
checklist.done: current certificates evidencing cyber, professional and ERISA bond cover at contracted limits are on file with expiry reminders set.

checklist.step: Onboard the provider and provision access on least privilege
actions: Create the provider's users as federated identities with MFA enforced and named sponsors, never as shared accounts.
Grant only the entitlements the service description requires and record the mapping from service to entitlement.
Register the provider's users in the quarterly access certification campaign with the sponsor as certifier.
Confirm the data interface goes over the agreed encrypted channel and that test data is masked.
checklist.done: provider access is federated, MFA-enforced, least-privilege, sponsor-owned and enrolled in the certification campaign.

checklist.step: Run the annual reassessment for Tier 1 providers
actions: Launch the reassessment 120 days before the contract anniversary so findings can be worked before renewal.
Collect the current SOC 2 Type II with a bridge letter covering any period gap, the latest penetration test summary and the incident log for the year.
Re-issue the security questionnaire and compare answers to last year's, challenging every changed answer and every unchanged answer where the environment demonstrably changed.
Verify the complementary user entity controls the report assumes and confirm the company performs each one.
Write the reassessment conclusion with a residual risk rating and a recommendation to renew, renew with conditions, or exit.
checklist.done: each Tier 1 provider has a dated annual reassessment with current SOC coverage, a residual risk rating and a renewal recommendation.

checklist.step: Drive provider findings to closure
actions: Log each finding from the SOC report, questionnaire or penetration test as a GRC item with severity, the provider's remediation commitment and a due date.
Require evidence of closure - a retest result or a configuration export - not a provider email saying it is fixed.
Escalate any critical finding open past 30 days to the Head of Compliance and to the relationship owner for a contractual remedy.
Report open findings by provider into the quarterly vendor risk pack for the plan committee.
checklist.done: every provider finding is tracked with severity, a due date and evidence-backed closure, with criticals escalated past 30 days.

checklist.step: Monitor the provider continuously between assessments
actions: Review the monthly SLA pack against the contract service levels and log every miss with its service credit position.
Monitor external signals - breach disclosures, regulatory actions, credit downgrades and adverse media - and open an out-of-cycle assessment when one lands.
Log every incident the provider reports with the notification time against the contracted 24-hour clock.
Hold a quarterly service review with the provider and the Retirement Operations Administrator and minute the actions.
checklist.done: SLA misses, external risk signals and provider-reported incidents are logged monthly with a minuted quarterly service review.

checklist.step: Capture provider change disclosures inside 60 days
actions: Log the date the provider informed the company of any change to its services, fiduciary status or compensation, including revenue sharing changes.
Compute the disclosure due date as that date plus 60 days under 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1)(v) and set the amber alert at 45 days.
Chase the written disclosure and record the received date, then update the compensation record used for the reasonableness determination and Schedule C.
Escalate any change disclosure still outstanding at 60 days to the Head of Compliance as a prohibited transaction risk.
checklist.done: every provider change has a logged notification date, a computed 60-day due date and a received written disclosure or an escalation.

checklist.step: Answer fiduciary information requests inside 30 days
actions: Log every request from a responsible plan fiduciary for information needed to comply with the reporting and disclosure rules, with the request date.
Compute the due date as request date plus 30 days under 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1)(vi) and set an amber alert at day 20.
Assemble the response from the compensation record and the service description and have it reviewed before release.
Record the response date and content against the request and escalate anything approaching day 30 to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: each fiduciary information request has a logged date, a computed 30-day due date and a recorded response inside the window.

checklist.step: Document the fiduciary reasonableness determination
actions: Benchmark the provider's total direct and indirect compensation against market data for comparable services and plan size, and cite the benchmarking source and date.
Set out the services actually received against the compensation paid and record the committee's reasoning, not just its vote.
Include the security assessment conclusion so cyber quality is visibly part of the prudence record required by ERISA 404(a)(1)(B).
Take the determination to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and record the minute reference against the provider.
checklist.done: a benchmarked, minuted reasonableness determination citing services, compensation and the security assessment exists per provider.

checklist.step: Run the exit: terminate access, return and destroy data
actions: On notice of termination trigger the exit checklist: transition plan with dates, final data extract in the agreed format, and the access revocation date.
Disable every provider identity in the IAM platform on the revocation date and confirm no residual entitlement remains after 24 hours.
Obtain the signed certificate of destruction covering all copies including backups, within the contracted number of days.
Confirm with the Retirement Operations Administrator that the receiving provider holds a complete participant record set before the outgoing provider deletes anything.
checklist.done: access is revoked on the agreed date, a complete record set is proven at the receiving provider, and a signed destruction certificate is on file.

checklist.step: Retain the oversight file for the retention period
actions: File per provider: due diligence pack, 408(b)(2) disclosures and change disclosures, contracts and amendments, SOC reports and bridge letters, questionnaires, findings and closure evidence, benchmarking and the reasonableness determination.
Apply a 6-year ERISA 107 retention label running from contract termination rather than from creation.
Index by provider name, plan number and contract anniversary so an EBSA request can be answered by provider or by plan.
Run an annual completeness check that every register entry has a filed oversight folder.
checklist.done: every provider has a complete oversight folder retained 6 years from termination, indexed by provider and plan.

testing.step: Build the population of covered service providers for the year
actions: Extract from the vendor master every supplier paid from plan assets or charged to a plan during the year, with spend and service category.
Extract from Icertis every contract naming a plan, with execution, renewal and termination dates.
Add sub-custodians and subcontractors named in Tier 1 contracts so a flow-down provider cannot be missed.
Record the population counts, the extraction queries and the timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the provider population is extracted from spend and contract systems with subcontractors added, counts and queries recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the provider register
actions: Match every extracted provider to a register entry and list providers with spend or a contract but no register entry.
Match every register entry to a contract and list register entries with no executed contract.
Reconcile the count of Tier 1 providers to the count of completed annual reassessments and explain each gap.
Treat unmatched rows as completeness exceptions rather than adding them to the register mid-test.
testing.done: spend, contracts and the register reconcile three ways, with every unmatched provider recorded as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Tier 1 providers and 100% of new engagements, renewals and terminations in the year.
Take 15 Tier 2 providers at random using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note the obligation each sampled provider is being tested against.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Tier 1 providers and all contract events in the year is drawn with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the 408(b)(2) disclosure completeness review
actions: For each sampled contract open the disclosure and check it names the services, fiduciary or registered investment adviser status, and every element of direct and indirect compensation with payer, payee and formula.
Compare the disclosure date to the contract execution date and record any disclosure dated after execution as a prohibited transaction exposure.
Compare disclosed compensation to what was actually paid in the year from the accounts payable ledger and to Schedule C reporting.
Record a generic services description with no compensation formula as a fail, not a documentation weakness.
testing.done: every sampled contract has a pre-execution disclosure naming services, status and compensation that agrees to amounts actually paid.

testing.step: Re-perform the security assessment conclusion on Tier 1 providers
actions: Open the SOC 2 Type II report yourself and reach your own view on the exceptions before reading the assessor's conclusion.
Confirm the report period plus bridge letter covers the full year and that the trust services criteria in scope include security and confidentiality.
Check each complementary user entity control is mapped to an internal control that was evidenced this year.
Record any difference between your conclusion and the recorded residual risk rating as an exception, including where the right rating rests on the wrong evidence.
testing.done: each Tier 1 assessment carries an independent re-performance of the SOC review with period coverage and user entity controls verified.

testing.step: Trace access and data flows to the contracted scope
actions: For each sampled provider list its active identities and entitlements and compare them to the service description in the contract.
Confirm every identity is federated with MFA and has a named internal sponsor, and flag any shared account.
Compare the data elements actually flowing on the interface to those the contract and the tiering record permit - undisclosed SSN or bank detail flow is a fail.
For terminated providers confirm all identities were disabled on the revocation date and no access occurred afterwards.
testing.done: provider access and data flows are traced to contracted scope, with terminated providers proven disabled on the revocation date.

testing.step: Recompute the 60-day and 30-day disclosure clocks
actions: For each logged provider change recompute the due date as notification date plus 60 days and compare it to the disclosure received date.
For each fiduciary information request recompute the due date as request date plus 30 days and compare it to the response date.
Independently look for unlogged changes by comparing this year's compensation and service descriptions to last year's - a changed fee with no change log entry is an exception.
List every breach with the elapsed days and the provider name.
testing.done: both clocks are recomputed per event, unlogged changes are searched for independently, and every breach is listed with elapsed days.

testing.step: Test the reasonableness determination and its benchmarking
actions: For each sampled provider open the reasonableness determination and confirm it cites a dated benchmarking source and comparable plan size and service scope.
Confirm the determination pre-dates the contract or renewal it supports and carries a committee minute reference.
Confirm the security assessment conclusion is reflected, so the prudence record covers cyber quality and not only price.
Record a determination that only records a vote, with no reasoning, as a fail against ERISA 404(a)(1)(B).
testing.done: each sampled determination is dated before its contract, cites benchmarking and security findings, and records reasoning with a minute reference.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the provider, the contract, the failed obligation and the plan affected.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (provider not registered, disclosure not obtained, SOC gap, clause missing, clock missed, access beyond scope) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missing or late 408(b)(2) disclosure, open a prohibited transaction assessment with Legal Counsel including the correction and relief route.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly interim test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner and remediation date, with prohibited transaction assessments opened where disclosure failed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the proportion of Tier 1 providers with full-year SOC coverage and the count of contracts entered without a pre-execution disclosure.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing provider names and workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer - who performed none of the sampled assessments and owns no sampled relationship - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any prohibited transaction exposure to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage statistics, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the plan document and SPD library for every ERISA plan the company sponsors or administers, and owns the amendment-to-SPD-to-system conformity chain

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - ERISA 402(a) written instrument and 404(a)(1)(D) documents-and-instruments duty, with 29 CFR 2520.102-3(t) on required SPD claims-procedure content and 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) on the consequence of failing to follow reasonable claims procedures, re-read at each amendment

In-scope processes.value: Plan design change intake through legal drafting, adoption, SPD and SMM conformity, recordkeeping-system configuration and participant distribution, for the 401(k), group health, group life, group disability and group long-term care plans

In-scope systems.value: The plan document library with version control, DocuSign for adoption signatures, the payroll/benefits recordkeeping platform holding the administrative configuration, and the participant portal that publishes the SPD

Compliance procedure documented.value: Plan Document Control Procedure: change intake, counsel drafting, board or delegate adoption before the operational effective date, SPD and SMM conformity check, system configuration reconciliation, distribution and 30-day document request handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel; reviewed annually against IRS required-amendment and cycle guidance and after any legislative change such as SECURE-style amendment deadlines

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: SPD to a new participant within 90 days of coverage beginning and within 120 days of a plan first becoming subject to ERISA; SMM within 210 days after the plan year in which the change was adopted; restated SPD every 5 years where amended, otherwise every 10; documents to a written request within 30 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workflow tasks fire on amendment adoption at T+30 for the SMM draft and T+150 for issue, so the 210-day statutory date is never the first alert; a 20-day amber on every open 104(b)(4) document request; a 5-year restatement reminder per plan

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed plan documents and amendments, all SPD and SMM versions with distribution logs, the conformity checklists and the system configuration reconciliations retained 6 years under ERISA 107 and for the life of the plan for the governing instruments

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Operation ahead of adoption, SPD language conflicting with the plan document, a late SMM, and any document request answered after 30 days is logged with the plan number, participants affected and remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Employment Counsel signs off every scrivener's error correction, every retroactive amendment and every decision to administer a plan against literal document language

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All plan amendments adopted in the year, all SPD and SMM versions issued, and all 104(b)(4) document requests received, across every ERISA plan the company sponsors or administers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero amendments operated before adoption; zero SMMs issued after the 210-day date; zero conflicts between SPD language and plan document text on benefit, eligibility or claims terms; any document request answered after 30 days is a fail given the 110 dollars per day penalty exposure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; the test runs semi-annually over the amendments and notices issued in that half, plus an annual full-library conformity sweep before the plan year opens

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The reviewer must not have drafted, adopted or configured any sampled amendment

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual plan document conformity test workpaper (amendment population, adoption trace, SPD-to-document comparison, system reconciliation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Documents / <plan year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Current plan document with all amendments in adoption order, current SPD and every SMM with distribution proof, and the document request log, producible for an EBSA investigation or a participant claim file within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Employment Counsel responds to EBSA document requests and to participant attorney demands; the Chief HR Officer approves any voluntary correction filing, and Legal Counsel clears any statement about how the plan has actually been administered

checklist.step: Maintain the plan document inventory and the restatement cycle
actions: List every ERISA plan with plan number, EIN, plan year end, document type (individually designed, pre-approved document with opinion letter, wrap document) and the current restatement date.
Record for each plan the location of the executed base document, every amendment in adoption order, the trust agreement and the insurance contracts or certificates incorporated by reference.
Record the SPD version currently in force and its issue date, plus every SMM issued since that SPD.
Set the restatement reminder: 5 years from the last SPD where the plan has been amended, 10 years where it has not, and the pre-approved document cycle date where applicable.
Reconcile the inventory to the Form 5500 filing list so no plan exists in one and not the other.
checklist.done: every plan has an inventory row naming its executed document, amendment chain, SPD version, SMM list and next restatement date.

checklist.step: Take in plan design changes through a single intake
actions: Open a change record for every design decision - eligibility, match formula, vesting, distribution options, claims procedure, network or benefit schedule - regardless of who requested it.
Record the intended operational effective date, the population affected and the business sponsor.
Identify the driver: bargaining outcome, board decision, legislative requirement (for example a statutory amendment deadline), vendor change or correction of an operational failure.
Route every record to Employment Counsel for a drafting assessment before anything is communicated to employees.
Refuse changes whose operational date precedes any possible adoption date without a written retroactive-amendment analysis.
checklist.done: each design change has a record naming the effective date, affected population, driver and a counsel routing before any employee communication.

checklist.step: Draft the amendment
actions: Draft the amendment against the current executed document text, quoting the section replaced and the section as amended so the redline is unambiguous.
Check the change against the anti-cutback rule for accrued benefits and against nondiscrimination and coverage consequences flagged by the Benefits Analyst.
Confirm the amendment procedure in the plan document itself is followed - who may amend, in what form and with what notice.
Where the change is required by statute, state the required amendment deadline in the drafting memo so adoption is not scheduled past it.
Deliver the draft with a memo naming the sections touched, the SPD paragraphs that must change and the system settings that must change.
checklist.done: a redlined amendment plus a memo naming the affected SPD paragraphs and system settings is delivered by counsel.

checklist.step: Adopt the amendment with authorised signature before the operational date
actions: Confirm the signer holds the amendment authority the plan document grants (board, committee or delegated officer) and obtain the board or committee resolution where required.
Circulate for signature through DocuSign so the signature identity and execution date are captured and cannot be back-dated.
Check the executed date is on or before the operational effective date; where it is not, stop and route to counsel for a retroactive amendment analysis before administration continues.
File the executed amendment into the plan document library as the next sequential amendment with the resolution attached.
Record the adoption in the committee minutes with the minute reference stored against the amendment.
checklist.done: the amendment is signed by an authorised person with a captured execution date on or before the operational date, filed and minuted.

checklist.step: Conform the SPD language to the amended document
actions: Work the counsel memo paragraph by paragraph and edit each affected SPD section, keeping the SPD in the plain language an average participant can understand as ERISA 102 requires.

Re-check the SPD still contains every required element: plan name and number, plan sponsor and administrator with address, agent for service of process, eligibility and benefit terms, circumstances causing loss of benefits, amendment and termination rights, and ERISA rights statement.
Confirm the claims and appeals section still meets 29 CFR 2520.102-3(t): how to file, the time limits, the review procedure, and the right to bring a civil action under ERISA 502(a).
Produce a side-by-side of old SPD text, new SPD text and the governing plan document text and have counsel initial it.
checklist.done: a counsel-initialled side-by-side shows each amended SPD paragraph agreeing with the plan document and the 102-3(t) content intact.

checklist.step: Draft the Summary of Material Modifications and time it
actions: Draft the SMM describing the modification in plain language with its effective date and the plan it amends.
Compute the deadline as 210 days after the end of the plan year in which the modification was adopted, and set the internal issue date at least 60 days earlier.
For a group health plan check whether the change is a material reduction in covered services, which must be furnished within 60 days of adoption instead.
Have Employment Counsel approve the SMM wording and record the approval date.
Register the computed deadline and the internal issue date on the notice calendar.
checklist.done: an approved SMM exists with its 210-day statutory deadline computed and an earlier internal issue date on the calendar.

checklist.step: Verify the claims and appeals procedure content
actions: Read the plan document and SPD claims sections against 29 CFR 2560.503-1: the decision periods, the content of an adverse benefit determination, the right to records free of charge and the appeal timeframe.

For disability claims confirm the enhanced requirements: independence and impartiality of decision makers, disclosure of new evidence before a final decision, and the contractual limitations period stated in the denial notice.

Confirm the document does not purport to shorten a statutory deadline or to require exhaustion of a procedure that does not comply, given 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) deems exhaustion satisfied where procedures fail.
Record the review conclusion and any required document change with a date.
checklist.done: the claims sections are confirmed against 2560.503-1 including the disability enhancements, with any required change recorded and dated.

checklist.step: Issue the initial or restated SPD on the statutory clock
actions: For a new plan or a plan newly subject to ERISA, issue the SPD within 120 days of the plan becoming subject to ERISA.
For each new participant, issue the SPD within 90 days of coverage beginning, driven off the Workday HCM enrolment date rather than a manual list.
Restate the SPD every 5 years where amendments have been made, otherwise every 10, and record the issue date against the plan inventory.
Confirm each issued SPD carries its own issue date on the document so a participant can tell which version governed at a point in time.
checklist.done: SPDs are issued inside the 120-day, 90-day and 5 or 10 year clocks, each carrying a visible issue date, logged against the plan.

checklist.step: Reconcile the amended terms to the recordkeeping system configuration
actions: Take the counsel memo's list of settings and open each configuration screen: eligibility service rule, entry dates, match formula and true-up, vesting schedule, compensation definition, loan and hardship rules, and distribution options.
Compare the configured value to the amended document text word for word and record the screen capture with the comparison.
Book the configuration change to take effect on the amendment's effective date, not on the deployment date, and test it in the non-production environment against three sample participants.
Where configuration cannot express the document, raise it to Employment Counsel before go-live - administering differently from the document is a fiduciary breach under ERISA 404(a)(1)(D).
File the reconciliation with the amendment.
checklist.done: every setting named in the counsel memo is compared to document text with a captured screen and tested on sample participants before go-live.

checklist.step: Reconcile the SPD to the insurance contracts and certificates
actions: For the group life, disability, health and long-term care plans, compare the SPD benefit schedule to the group policy and certificate of coverage in force.
Confirm any wrap document correctly incorporates the certificates by reference and names the current policy numbers and effective dates.
Raise a policy amendment request with the carrier where the certificate lags the plan design decision, and track it to issue.
Record the comparison and its date against the plan inventory.
checklist.done: the SPD benefit schedule agrees to the in-force certificate for every insured plan, with carrier amendments tracked where it does not.

checklist.step: Version, approve and publish the documents
actions: Check the new SPD or SMM in as a new version with the plan number, version number, issue date and superseded version recorded.
Lock the superseded version read-only rather than deleting it - the version in force on a claim date must remain retrievable.
Publish the current SPD and all SMMs to the participant portal and confirm the links resolve for a test participant account.
Record the approver and publication date in the version history.
checklist.done: the new version is checked in with an issue date, the prior version is retained read-only, and the portal serves the current set.

checklist.step: Distribute and log delivery
actions: Build the recipient population from the recordkeeping platform: participants, beneficiaries receiving benefits and alternate payees under a QDRO.
Deliver by a method reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt - electronic delivery only for participants covered by the 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 safe harbour, with paper to everyone else.
Record counts sent, delivered, bounced and re-mailed, and re-issue on paper for every failed electronic delivery.
Retain the mailing file, the electronic delivery report and a specimen of the delivered document with its issue date.
checklist.done: delivery is logged with sent, delivered and bounced counts, failed electronic deliveries re-issued on paper, and a specimen retained.

checklist.step: Answer 104(b)(4) document requests within 30 days
actions: Log every written request from a participant, beneficiary or their representative with the receipt date and the documents requested.
Compute the due date as receipt plus 30 days and set an amber alert at day 20 - the ERISA 502(c)(1) penalty runs at up to 110 dollars per day beyond it.
Assemble the set: current plan document, trust agreement, current SPD, latest annual report and any contracts under which the plan is established or operated.
Send by a tracked method, record the send date and retain the cover letter and the enclosure list.
Escalate anything unfulfilled at day 20 to Employment Counsel.
checklist.done: each request has a logged receipt date, a computed 30-day due date and a tracked despatch with an enclosure list inside the window.

checklist.step: Run the annual full-library conformity sweep
actions: Before the plan year opens, take each plan's executed document plus every amendment in adoption order and read it against the SPD in force.
Check no amendment is missing from the chain, no amendment was adopted after its operational date without a counsel analysis, and no SMM is outstanding past 210 days.
Sample 10 administrative decisions per plan from the year and confirm each was made on the document terms then in force.
Produce a conformity report per plan with findings, owners and dates and take it to the plan committee.
checklist.done: each plan has an annual conformity report covering amendment chain completeness, SMM timeliness and sampled administrative decisions.

checklist.step: Retain the documents for the retention period
actions: File executed base documents, every amendment with its resolution, every SPD and SMM version with distribution logs, conformity checklists and system reconciliations.
Apply the ERISA 107 6-year label to the supporting records and an indefinite label to the governing instruments, which must be producible for as long as any benefit claim can arise.
Index by plan number, document type and effective date so the version governing a given claim date can be retrieved.
Apply legal hold to any plan with pending litigation or an EBSA inquiry.
checklist.done: governing instruments are retained indefinitely and supporting records for 6 years, retrievable by plan number and effective date, with holds applied.

testing.step: Build the population of amendments, SPDs, SMMs and document requests
actions: Extract every document checked into the plan document library in the period with plan number, document type, version, issue date and approver.
Extract the design change records and committee minutes for the period so an adopted change with no filed amendment is visible.
Extract the 104(b)(4) request log with receipt and response dates.
Record the population counts, extraction queries and timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: amendment, SPD, SMM and request populations are extracted with counts, queries and timestamps recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Reconcile committee minutes and design change records to filed amendments and list every adopted change with no executed document.
Reconcile the plan inventory to the Form 5500 filing list so a filed plan cannot be absent from the document library.
Reconcile the SMM list to the amendment list - every amendment either has an SMM or a documented reason it needs none.
Explain every difference in writing before sampling.
testing.done: minutes, amendments, SMMs and the 5500 plan list reconcile, with every difference explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of amendments affecting benefit accrual, eligibility, vesting or claims procedures, and 100% of document requests.
Take 12 further amendments or SMMs at random using a recorded seed, plus 10 administrative decisions per sampled plan.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note the obligation each sampled item tests.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all benefit-affecting amendments and all document requests is drawn with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the adoption-before-operation check
actions: For each sampled amendment read the DocuSign execution certificate for the signer identity and the signature timestamp.
Compare the execution timestamp to the operational effective date recorded on the change record and to the date the recordkeeping system configuration actually changed.
Confirm the signer held the amendment authority the plan document grants and that the resolution exists where required.
Record any amendment operated before adoption as an ERISA 404(a)(1)(D) breach, not a documentation lag.
testing.done: each sampled amendment has a verified authorised signature timestamp compared to both the operational date and the system change date.

testing.step: Re-perform the SPD-to-plan-document comparison
actions: Read the sampled SPD sections against the governing document text yourself before looking at the side-by-side prepared by the performer.
Check the required SPD content elements are all present and that the claims section meets 29 CFR 2520.102-3(t) and the 2560.503-1 disability enhancements.

Flag every conflict on eligibility, benefit amount, vesting or claims deadlines - a conflict favouring the SPD is a participant-communication exposure and a conflict favouring the document is a disclosure failure.
Capture the compared paragraphs into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled SPD sections are independently compared to document text with required content and claims-procedure elements confirmed.

testing.step: Trace administrative practice back to the governing text
actions: For each sampled administrative decision - an eligibility determination, a vesting calculation, a match true-up, a hardship approval - open the participant record and recompute the outcome from the document terms in force on that date.
Compare your recomputation to what the system produced and record the difference in dollars and in participants affected.
Where the system followed a configuration that does not match the document, quantify the population exposed and escalate immediately.
Capture the configuration screen and the participant record into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled decision is recomputed from the governing text, with any difference quantified in dollars and participants affected.

testing.step: Recompute the SMM, SPD and document request clocks
actions: For each sampled SMM recompute the deadline as 210 days after the end of the plan year of adoption, or 60 days from adoption for a material reduction in group health services, and compare it to the issue date.
For a sample of 25 new participants recompute the SPD due date as 90 days from coverage start using the Workday HCM enrolment date and compare it to the delivery log.
For each document request recompute receipt plus 30 days and compare it to the despatch date, then compute the potential ERISA 502(c)(1) penalty days at 110 dollars per day.
List every breach with the elapsed days, the plan number and the participants affected.
testing.done: all three clocks are recomputed from source dates, breaches are listed with elapsed days, and penalty exposure is quantified.

testing.step: Test distribution evidence and version retrievability
actions: For each sampled issue take the distribution log and confirm sent, delivered and bounced counts reconcile to the recipient population from the recordkeeping platform.
Confirm every failed electronic delivery was re-issued on paper and that electronic recipients were covered by the 2520.104b-31 safe harbour with its initial paper notice on file.
Pick three past claim dates and confirm the SPD version in force on each date can still be retrieved read-only from the repository.
Record any population gap, unre-issued bounce or unretrievable version as an exception.
testing.done: distribution counts reconcile to the recipient population, bounces are proven re-issued, and historic SPD versions are retrievable by date.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan number, document, participants affected and the dollar exposure where quantified.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (adopted late, SPD not conformed, configuration mismatch, SMM missed, request unanswered, version not retained) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any operational failure against document terms, open a correction assessment with Employment Counsel covering the EPCRS or VFCP route and participant make-whole.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner, remediation date and a correction assessment where the plan was mis-administered.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate on adoption timing, SPD conformity and notice deadlines against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing plan numbers and workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer - who drafted, adopted or configured none of the sampled amendments - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any mis-administration exposure to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with exception rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

In-scope processes.value: Annual reporting for every 401(k), group health, group life, group disability and long-term care plan the company sponsors, and Schedule A data the company issues as insurance carrier to other plans' administrators

In-scope systems.value: The filing calendar and status tracker feeding the EFAST2 web portal or the approved third-party filing software, with financial data drawn from the ERP general ledger and participant counts from the payroll/benefits recordkeeping platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Form 5500 Preparation and Filing Procedure: plan inventory, large or small plan determination, participant count as at the first day of the plan year, schedule assembly, audit engagement, reconciliation, EFAST2 credential control, electronic signature and acceptance verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and the Chief HR Officer; refreshed each January against the new plan year Form 5500 Instructions and any EFAST2 schema change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Filing due the last day of the seventh month after plan year end - 31 July for a calendar plan year - extendable by two and a half months to 15 October on a timely Form 5558; annual funding notice within 120 days of plan year end; Summary Annual Report within nine months of plan year end or two months after the extended filing date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar tasks at 31 March (data cut), 31 May (draft complete), 30 June (audit report due), 15 July (sign-off) against the 31 July date, and an automatic Form 5558 decision checkpoint at 10 July per plan

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late or rejected filing, an unfiled schedule, an unresolved EFAST2 error code or a Schedule A not received from a carrier is logged with the plan number, the days late and the DFVCP decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance approves every DFVCP submission and every amended Form 5500, and signs off the root cause before the next filing season opens

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ERISA plan required to file a Form 5500 or 5500-SF for the plan year, with its filed return, schedules, attachments and EFAST2 acknowledgement

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero plans filed after the applicable 31 July or extended 15 October date; zero large plans filed without an accountant's report; any Schedule H financial line not tied to the trust statement, and any participant count differing from the recordkeeping extract, is a fail

checklist.step: Build the plan inventory and the filing calendar for the plan year
actions: List every ERISA plan with its three-digit plan number, sponsor EIN, plan year end, plan type and whether it is funded through a trust or through insurance contracts.
Identify plans exempt from filing - unfunded or insured welfare plans with fewer than 100 participants at the start of the plan year - and record the exemption basis rather than simply omitting them.
Compute the base due date as the last day of the seventh month after plan year end and load it per plan, with the extended 15 October date noted.
Add mergers, terminations and new plans in the year, since a terminated plan still files a final return for its short plan year with the final-return box ticked.
Publish the calendar to the Controller, the Tax Manager and the plan auditors.
checklist.done: every plan has a calendar row with plan number, EIN, plan year, filing obligation or exemption basis, base and extended due dates.

checklist.step: Confirm the filing identifiers and plan characteristics
actions: Pull last year's filed return and carry forward the EIN, plan number, plan name and plan effective date exactly - a changed plan number creates a phantom unfiled plan in EBSA's records.

Select the plan characteristic codes on Form 5500 line 8 from the current instructions for the actual features in force (for example 2J participant-directed, 2K automatic enrolment, 3D pre-approved document).
Confirm the business code and the sponsor address against the current corporate records.
Have the Compensation & Benefits Manager review every changed identifier before the return is built.
checklist.done: identifiers agree to the prior filing or have a documented reason to change, and characteristic codes match the features actually in force.

checklist.step: Determine large or small plan status and the audit requirement
actions: Take the participant count as at the first day of the plan year - for defined contribution plans the count of participants with an account balance under the current counting method.
Apply the 80-120 rule: a plan that filed as small last year and has between 80 and 120 participants may continue filing as small, and record the election.
Set the filing form accordingly: Form 5500 with Schedule H and an accountant's report for a large plan, Form 5500-SF or Schedule I for a small plan.
Where an audit is required, confirm the engagement letter with the independent qualified public accountant is signed by 31 March.
Record the determination and its inputs so the conclusion can be re-performed.
checklist.done: each plan's large or small status, 80-120 election and audit requirement is determined from a dated participant count and recorded.

checklist.step: Extract and validate the participant counts
actions: Extract beginning-of-year and end-of-year counts by category: active participants, retired or separated participants receiving benefits, separated participants entitled to future benefits, and deceased participants with beneficiaries receiving benefits.
Extract the count of participants with account balances at the beginning and end of year for the defined contribution lines.
Reconcile the year-on-year movement to enrolments, terminations and distributions and explain any variance over the agreed threshold.
Extract the number of participants who terminated with a vested balance for the Form 8955-SSA and hand it to the Tax Manager.
Sign the extract with the run date and parameters used.
checklist.done: signed participant count extracts by category reconcile to enrolment and distribution activity with variances explained.

checklist.step: Assemble the trust financial data for Schedule H or I
actions: Obtain the trustee or custodian year-end statement and the full-year transaction activity for each plan trust.

Build the Schedule H asset categories: interest-bearing cash, registered investment company shares, employer securities, common collective trusts, pooled separate accounts, insurance company general account contracts and participant loans.

Build the income and expense lines: contributions received from employer and participants, interest, dividends, realised and unrealised gains, benefit payments, corrective distributions, administrative expenses and fees paid.
Prepare the supplemental schedules the instructions require, including the Schedule of Assets Held at End of Year and the Schedule of Reportable Transactions where applicable.
Prepare the delinquent participant contribution line and the accompanying schedule for any late deposit, since this line drives EBSA enforcement attention.
checklist.done: Schedule H or I lines and the supplemental schedules are built from trustee statements with the delinquent contribution line explicitly addressed.

checklist.step: Collect Schedule A from every insurer
actions: Write to each insurance carrier by 15 April requesting the Schedule A information the carrier must furnish under ERISA 103(a)(2) for the plan year.
Check each Schedule A carries the carrier name and EIN, the NAIC code, the contract number, the policy period, premiums paid and the commissions and fees by broker with agency name and address.
Chase carriers that have not responded by 31 May and escalate to the Third-Party Risk Manager, since the plan administrator remains responsible for the filing.
Reconcile the premiums shown to the premiums paid per the general ledger and clear any difference.
Attach each Schedule A to the correct plan and confirm the count of Schedule As matches the count of contracts in force.
checklist.done: a complete Schedule A is on file for every in-force contract with commissions detailed and premiums reconciled to the ledger.

checklist.step: Assemble Schedule C service provider compensation
actions: For large plans list every service provider receiving 5,000 dollars or more in direct or indirect compensation from the plan during the year.
Pull the direct compensation from the accounts payable ledger and the plan's expense account, and pull the indirect compensation from the 408(b)(2) disclosures on file.
Record eligible indirect compensation where the alternative reporting conditions are met, and name the person who received the required disclosure.
Identify any provider that failed or refused to supply the information and complete the Schedule C Part I(c) listing - naming them is required, not optional.
Reconcile the Schedule C total to the plan's administrative expense line on Schedule H.
checklist.done: Schedule C lists every provider over the threshold with direct and indirect compensation reconciled to the Schedule H expense line.

checklist.step: Assemble the remaining schedules
actions: Prepare Schedule SB or MB for any defined benefit or pension risk transfer obligation with the enrolled actuary's signature and certification.
Prepare Schedule R for distributions, funding and the single-employer plan questions, taking the payer EIN and distribution counts from the recordkeeping platform.
Prepare Schedule D where the plan invests in a common collective trust, pooled separate account, master trust or 103-12 entity, quoting each entity's EIN and plan number.
Prepare Schedule G where the plan has loans in default, leases in default or non-exempt transactions - a blank Schedule G where a prohibited transaction exists is a false filing.
Deliver each schedule with the underlying calculation file to the preparer.
checklist.done: every required schedule is prepared and signed where certification is needed, each with its calculation file attached.

checklist.step: Engage and manage the plan audit
actions: Confirm the independent qualified public accountant's engagement letter, independence confirmation and licence are on file before fieldwork.
Decide and document whether the audit is a full-scope audit or an ERISA 103(a)(3)(C) audit relying on a carrier or trustee certification, and hold the certification before relying on it.
Set the fieldwork dates so the report is delivered by 30 June for a calendar-year plan, and track open audit requests weekly.
Read the draft report for a modified opinion or a reportable finding and resolve or disclose it before filing.
Attach the signed accountant's report to the return as a PDF in the format the instructions require.
checklist.done: a signed accountant's report of the documented scope is delivered by 30 June and attached to the return with findings resolved or disclosed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the return to the trust and the ledger before review
actions: Tie Schedule H beginning net assets to the prior year filed ending net assets and investigate any difference to the dollar.
Tie ending net assets to the trustee statement and to the audited financial statements.
Tie contributions to payroll remittance records and benefit payments to the distribution register.
Tie the participant loan balance to the recordkeeping loan report and the deemed distribution amounts to the 1099-R file.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the preparation file - an unreconciled return is not ready for signature.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation ties opening and closing net assets, contributions, distributions and loans to trustee, payroll and audited records.

checklist.step: Control the EFAST2 credentials and build the electronic filing
actions: Confirm the signer holds current EFAST2 credentials with the Filing Author and Filing Signer roles registered at efast.dol.gov, and that credentials are individual and not shared.
Build the filing in the EFAST2 web portal or approved third-party software, entering data from the reconciled preparation file rather than re-keying from drafts.
Attach the accountant's report, supplemental schedules and any required attachments in the accepted format with the required attachment naming.
Run the software's edit checks and clear every error and warning, documenting the reason for any warning left in place.
Produce the reviewer proof copy for the Compensation & Benefits Manager and the Controller.
checklist.done: the filing is built with all attachments, edit checks cleared, and a proof copy issued to the reviewers from individual EFAST2 credentials.

checklist.step: Decide and file the extension where needed
actions: At the 10 July checkpoint assess each plan's readiness: audit report received, schedules complete, reconciliation signed.
For any plan not ready, file Form 5558 with the IRS on or before 31 July to obtain the two and a half month extension to 15 October, and retain a copy in the plan file.
Record the extension against the plan on the filing calendar and reset the reminders to the extended date.
Do not treat the extension as routine - record the reason so the root cause is visible next season.
checklist.done: every plan not ready by 10 July has a timely Form 5558 on file with the reason recorded and reminders reset to 15 October.

checklist.step: Review, sign electronically and transmit
actions: Review the proof against the reconciliation and the schedules, focusing on participant counts, net assets, the delinquent contribution line and the Schedule C provider list.
Apply the electronic signature under penalty of perjury as plan administrator, using your own credentials - a signature applied by the preparer is invalid.
Transmit before the applicable 31 July or 15 October deadline and capture the submission timestamp.
Record the signer, the submission time and the plan number in the filing tracker immediately.
checklist.done: the return is reviewed, signed with the plan administrator's own EFAST2 credentials and transmitted before the applicable deadline with the timestamp captured.

checklist.step: Verify acceptance and clear any filing status error
actions: Retrieve the EFAST2 acknowledgement and record the filing ID and status - Filing Received, Filing Error or Filing Stopped.
Where the status is not accepted, read the error codes, correct the cause and re-transmit before the deadline; a rejected filing is an unfiled return.
Check the return appears in the EFAST2 Filing Search public disclosure record with the right plan number and plan year.
File the acknowledgement and the accepted return PDF against the plan and close the calendar row.
checklist.done: each plan has an EFAST2 acknowledgement with a filing ID and an accepted status, visible in the public filing search.

checklist.step: Distribute the SAR and remediate any late filing through DFVCP
actions: Produce the Summary Annual Report for each plan required to furnish one and distribute it within nine months of plan year end, or within two months after the extended filing date where Form 5558 was used.
Distribute the annual funding notice for any defined benefit plan within 120 days of plan year end under 29 CFR 2520.101-2.

For any plan filed late, prepare the Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program submission under 78 FR 5060 before EBSA issues a notice, and pay the reduced per-plan penalty rather than face ERISA 502(c)(2) exposure.
Log the late filing with days late, the DFVCP submission date and the root cause, and report it to the plan committee.
File the SAR distribution log and the DFVCP acknowledgement with the plan year file.
checklist.done: SARs and funding notices are distributed inside their clocks and every late filing has a DFVCP submission logged with its root cause.

testing.step: Build the population of plans required to file
actions: Extract the plan inventory with plan numbers, EINs and plan year ends, and independently corroborate it against the prior year EFAST2 filings for the same sponsor EIN.
Add plans established, merged or terminated in the year from the committee minutes and the plan document library, since these are the ones most often missed.
Extract the participant counts used for the large or small determination straight from the recordkeeping platform.
Record population counts, extraction method and timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the required-filer population is built from inventory, prior filings and committee minutes with counts and method recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to what was actually filed
actions: Search the EFAST2 public Filing Search by sponsor EIN for the plan year and list every plan number found.
Reconcile filings found to the required-filer population and investigate both directions - an unfiled plan and a filing for a plan not on the inventory.
Reconcile the exemption basis recorded for each non-filing plan to the participant count and funding method that support it.
Explain every difference in writing before sampling.
testing.done: filings retrieved from EFAST2 reconcile to the required-filer population in both directions with exemption bases verified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of large plans, 100% of final returns and 100% of plans reporting delinquent participant contributions.
Take 8 small plans at random using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
State which schedule and which assertion each sampled plan is being tested against.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all large plans, final returns and delinquent-contribution filers is drawn with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the large or small plan and audit determination
actions: Recompute the beginning-of-year participant count from the recordkeeping extract yourself, using the counting method in the current instructions.
Apply the 80-120 rule against the prior year filing status and reach your own conclusion before reading the recorded determination.
Confirm an accountant's report is attached for every plan your recomputation makes large.
Record any plan filed as small that should have been large as a fail, since the missing audit cannot be cured by a footnote.
testing.done: participant counts and the large or small conclusion are independently recomputed, with audit attachment confirmed for every large plan.

testing.step: Trace the return lines to the trust, ledger and payroll records
actions: Agree Schedule H beginning net assets to the prior year filed ending net assets and ending net assets to the trustee statement and the audited financial statements.
Agree contributions to the payroll remittance file and benefit payments to the distribution register and the 1099-R totals.
Agree the Schedule C total to the Schedule H administrative expense line and to the accounts payable detail.
Agree each Schedule A to the in-force contract list and the premiums to the ledger, and record any contract with no Schedule A.
testing.done: every sampled return line traces to trustee, ledger, payroll and contract records, with unmatched contracts recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the delinquent contribution test
actions: Extract every participant contribution remittance for the year with the payroll date and the trust deposit date.

Compute days from payroll withholding to deposit for each and identify remittances outside the earliest date the amounts could reasonably be segregated, applying the seven business day safe harbour only where the plan qualifies as small.
Compare your list of late remittances to the amount reported on the Schedule H delinquent contribution line and the supplemental schedule.
Confirm lost earnings were calculated and deposited and that any Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program filing exists, and record an understated line as a reportable exception.
testing.done: late remittances are independently identified and compared to the reported delinquent contribution line, with lost earnings and any VFCP filing confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute every filing deadline and the extension validity
actions: For each sampled plan recompute the base due date as the last day of the seventh month after plan year end from the plan year end on the return itself.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm the Form 5558 was filed on or before the base due date and recompute the extended date as two and a half months later.
Compare the EFAST2 submission timestamp to the applicable due date and record the days late for any breach.
For any late plan confirm a DFVCP submission exists and recompute the per-plan penalty cap claimed.
testing.done: base and extended due dates are recomputed per plan and compared to the submission timestamp, with days late and DFVCP status recorded.

testing.step: Verify acceptance, public disclosure and SAR distribution
actions: Open the EFAST2 acknowledgement for each sampled plan and confirm the status is accepted and the filing ID matches the retained return PDF.
Search the EFAST2 public filing record and confirm the filing is visible with the correct plan number, plan year and attachments.
Recompute the SAR due date as nine months after plan year end, or two months after the extended filing date, and compare it to the distribution log.
For any defined benefit plan recompute the annual funding notice date as 120 days after plan year end and compare it to the distribution log.
testing.done: each sampled filing is confirmed accepted and publicly visible, with SAR and funding notice dates recomputed against distribution logs.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan number, plan year, the failed element and the penalty exposure under ERISA 502(c)(2).
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (plan omitted from inventory, audit late, Schedule A not received, reconciliation break, extension missed, filing rejected and not re-sent) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the return was wrong, prepare an amended filing and a DFVCP or VFCP assessment with Legal Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next filing season's May readiness check as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner, remediation date and an amended filing or voluntary correction assessment where needed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate, the count of rejected filings and the value of delinquent contributions reported against the population.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing plan numbers, filing IDs and workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer - who prepared, reviewed or signed none of the sampled returns - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late or amended filing to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and the Audit Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time filing rate, a stated conclusion and committee reporting dates is filed in the evidence repository.
