checklist.step: Build the notice catalogue with the legal clock per notice
actions: List every participant notice the plans owe with its citation, trigger event, recipient population, deadline formula and owner.

Record for the 404a-5 suite: initial disclosure before first investment direction, annual disclosure at least once in any 14-month period, quarterly statement of fees actually charged, and advance notice of change at least 30 and not more than 90 days before the change.

Record the others: SPD within 90 days of coverage, SMM within 210 days of the plan year of adoption, blackout notice 30 to 60 days ahead, QDIA notice at least 30 days ahead, safe harbour notice 30 to 90 days before the plan year, and the 2560.503-1 claim and appeal notices.
Have Employment Counsel verify each deadline formula against the current regulation text and date the verification.
Publish the catalogue as the single source for the notice calendar.
checklist.done: a counsel-verified catalogue lists every notice with its citation, trigger, recipients, deadline formula and owner.

checklist.step: Load the annual notice calendar and wire it to system triggers
actions: Load each recurring notice onto the calendar with its statutory date and an internal production date at least 45 days earlier.

Wire the event-driven notices to system events rather than to human memory: enrolment creates the SPD and initial disclosure task, a fund line-up change creates the 30-day notice task, a conversion project creates the blackout task.
Set the annual 404a-5 date so the gap from the prior year's issue date never exceeds 14 months, and record the prior issue date on the calendar row.
Assign each calendar row an owner and a reviewer and publish it to the Retirement Operations Administrator and the print vendor.
checklist.done: every recurring and event-driven notice has a calendar row with an owner, an internal production date and an automatic system trigger.

checklist.step: Maintain the participant address and delivery-method file
actions: Refresh participant mailing addresses from the Workday HCM feed for actives and run a national change of address and locator search for terminated participants and beneficiaries quarterly.
Maintain the electronic delivery eligibility flag per participant: wired-at-work eligible, 2520.104b-31 covered with an electronic address on file, or paper only.
Record for each e-delivery participant the initial paper notice date, the electronic address and any opt-out to paper, and honour opt-outs immediately.
Report the count of participants with no valid address or electronic address and work the missing participant procedure with the Benefits Administrator.
Freeze and sign the recipient file before each notice run.
checklist.done: a signed recipient file per run shows a valid delivery method for every participant, with missing addresses worked and opt-outs honoured.

checklist.step: Operate the electronic delivery safe harbour properly
actions: Before moving any participant to electronic delivery, send the paper initial notice under 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 stating the electronic address to be used, the right to request paper free of charge and the right to opt out entirely.
Send the notice of internet availability for each covered document, describing the document, where it is posted, how long it will remain available and the right to paper.
Monitor for invalid electronic addresses on every send and treat a bounce as a failed delivery requiring prompt paper re-issue.
Keep each posted document available on the portal for at least one year or until superseded, and record the posting and removal dates.
checklist.done: each e-delivery participant has a dated initial paper notice on file, notices of internet availability are issued, and bounces trigger paper re-issue.

checklist.step: Produce the 404a-5 plan-related disclosure
actions: Draft the general plan information: how to give investment instructions, any restrictions on instructions, the designated investment alternatives, any brokerage window and the voting and tender rights.
Draft the administrative expense information: the plan-level charges that may be deducted from accounts and how they will be allocated - pro rata or per capita.
Draft the individual expense information: loan origination, QDRO processing, distribution and advice fees, each with the amount actually charged.
Reconcile every stated fee to the current service agreements and the 408(b)(2) disclosures on file, since a disclosed fee that differs from the contract is a disclosure failure.
Have Employment Counsel approve the wording and record the approval date and version.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned plan-related disclosure states general, administrative and individual fee information reconciled to the service agreements.

checklist.step: Produce the comparative chart of designated investment alternatives
actions: Build the chart in the format 2550.404a-5(d)(2) requires: each alternative with its name, category, and one, five and ten year or since-inception average annual total returns against a named appropriate broad-based benchmark for the same periods.
Add the fee and expense table: total annual operating expenses as a percentage and per 1,000 dollars invested, plus shareholder-type fees and any restriction on purchase, transfer or withdrawal.
Add fixed-return alternatives with the annual rate of return, the term and the minimum rate.

Take the return, expense ratio and benchmark data as at the most recent quarter end from the fund fact sheets and reconcile to the recordkeeping platform's fund table so the chart and the participant's actual holdings agree.
Include the required website address for each alternative and the glossary reference, and test every link resolves.
checklist.done: a chart in the prescribed format shows returns against named benchmarks, expenses per 1,000 dollars and working websites, reconciled to the fund table.

checklist.step: Deliver the initial disclosure before the participant can first direct investments
actions: Take the daily new-eligible feed from the recordkeeping platform and compare each participant's first date they may direct investments to the disclosure send date.
Send the plan-related disclosure and the comparative chart on or before that date - not with the first statement.
Where automatic enrolment applies, deliver the QDIA notice at least 30 days before the first contribution is invested in the default alternative.
Log each send against the participant id with the date, method and document version, and re-run the comparison weekly to catch anyone missed.
checklist.done: every newly eligible participant has a logged initial disclosure and chart dated on or before the first direction date, with QDIA notice where applicable.

checklist.step: Deliver the annual disclosure inside the 14-month window
actions: Take the prior year's issue date per plan and compute the latest permissible annual issue date as prior issue date plus 14 months.
Schedule production so the send date is at least 45 days before that latest date, and confirm the chart data is as at the most recent quarter end.
Run the send against the frozen recipient file covering participants, beneficiaries with accounts and alternate payees.
Reconcile the send count to the recipient file count and investigate any shortfall before closing the run.
Record the new issue date on the calendar row so next year's window is computed from it.
checklist.done: the annual disclosure is issued inside the 14-month window with the send count reconciled to the recipient file and the issue date recorded.

checklist.step: Produce and issue the quarterly statement of fees actually charged
actions: Extract the administrative and individual charges actually deducted from each account in the quarter, with the date, description and dollar amount for each.
State on the statement the services to which each charge relates and, where applicable, that some plan expenses were paid from the total annual operating expenses of the investments.
Combine with the benefit statement so the participant receives both, and issue within 45 days of quarter end.
Reconcile the total of charges shown across all statements to the plan's fee revenue and expense accounts and clear any difference.
Log the run date, the account count and the delivery method split.
checklist.done: quarterly statements showing dated dollar charges by service are issued within 45 days of quarter end and reconciled to the plan expense accounts.

checklist.step: Issue advance notice of any change 30 to 90 days ahead
actions: Intercept every proposed change - fund addition or removal, share class change, fee change, recordkeeper change, restriction change - at the decision point, not at implementation.
Compute the notice window as at least 30 and not more than 90 days before the effective date and book the send date inside it.
Draft the change notice describing what changes, when, what the participant must do and the new fees or alternatives, and have counsel approve it.
Block the effective date in the change record until the notice send date is confirmed, so a fund can never map before participants are told.
Where the change is unforeseeable, document the reason and send as soon as reasonably practicable, recording the justification.
checklist.done: every change has a notice sent 30 to 90 days ahead, or a documented unforeseeable-event justification, with the effective date blocked until sent.

checklist.step: Issue blackout and QDIA notices on their own clocks
actions: For any conversion, fund mapping or recordkeeper transition, identify the blackout start and end dates and the affected rights.
Issue the blackout notice at least 30 and not more than 60 days before the blackout begins, stating the reasons, the rights suspended, the expected dates and the advice to review current investments.
Notify corporate officers separately where trading restrictions on employer securities apply, and coordinate with the Corporate Secretary.
Issue the annual QDIA notice at least 30 days before the start of each plan year for participants defaulted into the QDIA.
Log every send with dates and recipient counts and retain a specimen.
checklist.done: blackout notices are issued 30 to 60 days ahead with rights and dates stated, and annual QDIA notices are issued at least 30 days before the plan year.

checklist.step: Issue claim and appeal notices on the 2560.503-1 clocks
actions: Compute the decision deadline from the claim receipt date - 45 days for a disability claim with up to two 30-day extensions, and the shorter group health clocks for urgent and pre-service claims.
Where an extension is needed, issue the written extension notice before the original deadline expires, stating the reason and the expected decision date.

Write every adverse benefit determination with the specific reason, the plan provisions relied on, a description of additional material needed, the appeal procedure and the right to bring a civil action under ERISA 502(a).
For disability claims include the required disclosures on internal rules relied on, any medical or vocational expert consulted, and the contractual limitations period with its expiry date.
Log the receipt date, the decision date and the notice content version against each claim.
checklist.done: each claim shows a decision or a timely extension notice inside its statutory clock and an adverse determination containing every required element.

checklist.step: Log every delivery and work the bounces
actions: Capture per run: document name and version, recipient count, send date, delivery method split, delivered count, bounced count and returned mail count.
Match bounces and returned mail to participant records and trigger the address search and paper re-issue within 10 business days.
Retain a specimen of the exact document delivered with its version and issue date, not a template.
Publish a delivery summary per run to the Benefits Administrator and file it with the notice evidence.
checklist.done: each run has a delivery summary with sent, delivered, bounced and re-issued counts, and a retained specimen of the delivered document.

checklist.step: Remediate missed and failed notices
actions: Reconcile the notice calendar to the delivery logs weekly and open an issue for every notice not sent by its internal date.
For any statutory deadline already missed, quantify the participants affected and the exposure, and issue the notice immediately with a covering explanation.
Assess with Employment Counsel whether a corrective step beyond re-issue is required - for example an extended election window where a participant was denied an informed choice.
Record the root cause and change the trigger, the calendar or the recipient file so the same notice cannot be missed again.
Report missed notices to the plan committee with the participants affected.
checklist.done: every missed notice has an issue, an immediate re-issue, a counsel assessment of further correction and a changed control to prevent recurrence.

checklist.step: Retain the notice evidence for the retention period
actions: File per run: the approved specimen, the frozen recipient file, the delivery and bounce reports, the counsel approval and the calendar row showing the computed deadline.
File the e-delivery evidence: initial paper notices, notices of internet availability, opt-out records and portal posting and removal dates.
Apply the 6-year ERISA 107 retention label and index by plan number, notice type and issue date so the version a participant received on a given date can be produced.
Run an annual completeness check that every calendar row has a filed evidence pack.
checklist.done: every notice run has a complete evidence pack retained 6 years, retrievable by plan number, notice type and issue date.

testing.step: Build the population of notice events for the period
actions: Extract every newly eligible participant with the date they could first direct investments, every fund and fee change with its effective date, every blackout and every adverse benefit determination in the period.
Extract the account population for each quarterly statement run and the annual disclosure recipient population.
Independently corroborate the change population from the investment committee minutes and the recordkeeping platform's fund table history, so a change effected without a calendar row is visible.
Record the population counts, extraction queries and timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the notice event population is built from system events and corroborated against committee minutes, with counts and queries recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the event population to the notice calendar and delivery logs
actions: Match every event to a calendar row and every calendar row to a delivery log and list both kinds of orphan.
Reconcile each run's recipient count to the eligible population from the recordkeeping platform on the freeze date and explain any shortfall.
Confirm the number of quarterly statement runs equals four and that each covers the full account population.
Treat unmatched events as completeness exceptions rather than adjusting the population.
testing.done: every notice event reconciles to a calendar row and a delivery log with recipient counts agreed to the eligible population.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of fund and fee changes, 100% of blackouts and 100% of adverse disability determinations.
Take 40 newly eligible participants and 40 annual disclosure recipients at random using a recorded seed, plus 25 quarterly statements.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note which notice and which clock each sampled item tests.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all changes, blackouts and disability denials is drawn with the seed and dates recorded.

testing.step: Recompute every notice deadline from source dates
actions: For each sampled new participant compute the first-direction date from the recordkeeping eligibility record and compare it to the initial disclosure send date.
For the annual disclosure compute prior issue date plus 14 months and compare it to this year's send date.
For each quarterly statement compute quarter end plus 45 days and compare it to the run date.
For each change compute the days between the notice send date and the effective date and test it falls between 30 and 90; for each blackout test 30 to 60 days.
List every breach with the elapsed days, the plan number and the participants affected.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is recomputed from source system dates and compared to the actual send, with breaches listed in days.

testing.step: Re-perform the comparative chart content check
actions: Take the chart as issued and independently verify each alternative's one, five and ten year returns and expense ratio against the fund fact sheet as at the stated date.
Confirm a named appropriate broad-based benchmark is shown for each period, and that expenses appear both as a percentage and per 1,000 dollars invested.
Confirm every alternative on the recordkeeping platform's fund table appears on the chart and vice versa, and that each website address resolves.
Record stale data, a missing benchmark, a missing alternative or a dead link as a content exception.
testing.done: chart returns, expenses, benchmarks and websites are independently verified and the alternative list agrees to the fund table.

testing.step: Re-perform the quarterly fee statement calculation
actions: For each sampled statement extract the account's actual deductions for the quarter from the transaction history.
Recompute the total and compare it line by line to the amounts and descriptions printed on the statement.
Confirm each charge names the service it relates to and that plan-level allocations follow the disclosed pro rata or per capita method.
Reconcile the aggregate of sampled charges to the plan expense account and record any statement that omits a deducted charge as a fail.
testing.done: sampled statements are recomputed against actual account deductions with each charge matched to a named service and allocation method.

testing.step: Trace delivery evidence to identifiable participants
actions: For each sampled recipient confirm the delivery log names the participant id, the document version, the send date and the method.
For e-delivery recipients confirm the initial paper notice under 2520.104b-31 and the notice of internet availability exist and pre-date the send.
For every bounce in the sampled runs confirm a paper re-issue within 10 business days and a corrected address.
Confirm the retained specimen is the exact version delivered and not a later revision.
testing.done: each sampled delivery traces to a participant id, a dated version specimen, and valid e-delivery consent evidence or a paper re-issue.

testing.step: Re-perform the claim and appeal notice timing and content
actions: For each sampled adverse determination recompute the decision deadline from the receipt date under 29 CFR 2560.503-1 and compare it to the decision date.
Where an extension was used confirm the written extension notice pre-dates the original deadline and states the reason and the expected decision date.

Read the denial letter against the required content list including, for disability claims, the internal rules relied on, expert consultation and the contractual limitations period with its expiry date.
Record a missing 502(a) civil action statement or a missing limitations date as a content fail regardless of timing.
testing.done: each sampled denial is proven timely or properly extended and contains every required content element for its claim type.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan number, notice type, participants affected and the elapsed days beyond the deadline.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (trigger not wired, calendar row missing, recipient file stale, data source stale, bounce not worked, change effected early) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and open a counsel assessment where a participant was denied an informed choice, covering re-issue plus any corrective election window.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel assessment where participant choice was affected.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time rate per notice type and the count of participants affected by any late or missing notice.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing notice types, plan numbers and workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer - who produced, approved or distributed none of the sampled notices - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any participant-affecting failure to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rates by notice type, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual nondiscrimination testing cycle for the 401(k) and group plans and the documented prudent process behind each testing judgement and correction decision

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - ERISA 404(a)(1)(B) prudence read with IRC 410(b) coverage, 401(k)(3) ADP and 401(m)(2) ACP, 401(a)(4) general nondiscrimination, 416 top-heavy, 415(c) annual additions, 401(a)(17) compensation limit and 402(g) deferral limit, and the plan document's own definitions

In-scope processes.value: Annual compliance testing for the 401(k) and any related defined contribution plans across the controlled group: census assembly, HCE and key employee determination, coverage, ADP and ACP, general test, top-heavy, limit testing and correction

In-scope systems.value: The recordkeeping platform's testing module fed by the payroll census from ADP Payroll and the worker and ownership data from Workday HCM, with results and workpapers held in Microsoft Excel and filed in the evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Nondiscrimination Testing Procedure: census specification and validation rules, HCE and key employee determination, controlled group scope, test order and elections, correction hierarchy and the documented prudence record for every judgement

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel; re-approved annually before the census cut and whenever a plan amendment changes the compensation definition, match formula or safe harbour status

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Census cut 15 January; preliminary results by 15 February; ADP or ACP corrective distributions within 2.5 months of plan year end (15 March for a calendar plan year) to avoid the 10 percent employer excise tax, and in all events within 12 months to preserve qualification; 402(g) excess deferrals distributed by 15 April; QNEC funding by the 12-month date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar tasks at 15 January (census), 15 February (preliminary results), 1 March (correction decision) and 10 March (refund file to payroll) against the 15 March excise-tax date, with a second track running to 15 April for 402(g) and to 31 December for the 12-month backstop

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Census file with validation results, HCE and key employee determinations, every test run with its parameters and elections, the correction calculation and funding proof, retained 6 years under ERISA 107 and for the life of the plan for qualification support

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A failed test not corrected by 15 March, a census error found after testing, an exceeded 402(g) or 415(c) limit and any coverage failure is logged with the participants affected, the dollar impact and the correction route

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Employment Counsel signs off every correction method chosen, every EPCRS self-correction or VCP filing and any decision to rely on a testing election that changes a failing result to a passing one

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full plan year census for every plan and every controlled group member, all test runs performed, and every corrective distribution, forfeiture reallocation and QNEC made for the plan year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every required test run and either passed or corrected; zero corrections funded after the 12-month date; any census compensation field differing from payroll by more than the agreed tolerance, or any HCE determination not reproducible from the source data, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per plan year after the correction window closes, with a mid-year interim run in July using six months of census data to surface a likely ADP failure while it can still be managed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The reviewer must not have produced the census, run any test or calculated any correction for the year under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual nondiscrimination testing workpaper (census reconciliation, HCE re-performance, test recomputation, correction recalculation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Testing / <plan year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Census with validation evidence, HCE and key employee lists, signed test result packs with parameters and elections, correction calculations and funding proof, producible for an IRS plan examination or an EBSA investigation within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Tax Manager owns IRS examination correspondence on qualification and excise tax; Employment Counsel owns EPCRS and VCP submissions; Head of Compliance reports any failure that reached the 12-month backstop to the plan committee

checklist.step: Specify and cut the plan year census
actions: Publish the census specification: employee id, name, date of birth, date of hire, date of termination, rehire dates, hours of service, employment status, division and participating employer.
Add the ownership and family data the HCE and key employee tests need: percentage ownership, officer status and relationship to an owner for attribution.

Cut the census as at 15 January for the completed plan year, including employees who were eligible but did not defer and employees who terminated during the year - excluding them is the single most common testing error.
Run the validation rules: no missing birth or hire dates, no negative hours, no duplicate employee ids, no participant with deferrals but no compensation.
Sign the census with the cut date, the record count and the validation results and issue it to the Benefits Analyst.
checklist.done: a signed census covering every eligible employee including non-deferrers and terminees passes the validation rules with a recorded count.

checklist.step: Reconcile census compensation to payroll and to the plan definition
actions: Extract full-year gross wages, W-2 Box 1, and each pay component from ADP Payroll: base, overtime, bonus, commission, severance, imputed income, equity settlement and fringe benefits.

Build both compensation figures the tests need: total compensation under IRC 415(c)(3) and plan compensation under the plan document's own definition, including or excluding bonus and overtime exactly as the document says.
Reconcile total census compensation to the payroll general ledger control total and investigate every difference over the agreed tolerance.
Confirm deferrals and match amounts on the census tie to the remittance file and to the recordkeeping platform contribution history to the dollar.
Sign the reconciliation and attach the pay component mapping so the definition used is reproducible.
checklist.done: census compensation ties to payroll control totals and to the plan definition with a signed reconciliation and a documented component mapping.

checklist.step: Apply the statutory compensation and deferral limits
actions: Apply the IRC 401(a)(17) annual compensation limit for the plan year to every participant's plan compensation before any test is run.
Identify participants whose elective deferrals exceeded the IRC 402(g) limit for the calendar year, including catch-up eligibility for those aged 50 and over.
Aggregate deferrals across plans of the same employer and request from participants any deferrals made to an unrelated employer's plan, since the 402(g) limit is personal.
Schedule any excess deferral for distribution with allocable earnings by 15 April of the following year and hand the list to the Payroll Specialist.
Record the limit values used for the plan year on the workpaper cover sheet.
checklist.done: the 401(a)(17) limit is applied before testing and every 402(g) excess is identified with a 15 April distribution scheduled.

checklist.step: Determine the HCE and key employee populations
actions: Determine highly compensated employees on the lookback year: more than 5 percent owners in the current or lookback year, plus employees whose prior year compensation exceeded the statutory threshold.
Record whether the top-paid group election applies under the plan document and, if so, apply it consistently and document the ranking.
Apply family attribution under IRC 318 for ownership held by a spouse, child, grandchild or parent and show the attribution chain per person.

Determine key employees for top-heavy purposes on the determination date: officers above the compensation threshold, more than 5 percent owners and more than 1 percent owners with compensation over 150,000 dollars.
Have the Chief HR Officer confirm the officer list and file the determination with its source data.
checklist.done: reproducible HCE and key employee lists exist with ownership attribution chains, the top-paid group election applied consistently and the officer list confirmed.

checklist.step: Establish the controlled group and testing scope
actions: Confirm the controlled group under IRC 414(b) and (c) and any affiliated service group under 414(m) from the current legal entity and ownership structure, and date the analysis.
Confirm which entities participate in the plan and which employees of non-participating members must still be counted for coverage testing.
Record acquisitions and disposals in the year and whether the 410(b)(6)(C) transition rule applies, with its expiry date.
Decide and document any permissive aggregation or disaggregation - for example disaggregating employees who have not met statutory eligibility - and apply it to every test consistently.
Issue the scope memo to the testing team before any test is run.
checklist.done: a dated scope memo names the controlled group, participating and non-participating members, transition relief and the aggregation elections used.

checklist.step: Run the 410(b) coverage test
actions: Build the coverage populations: all employees of the controlled group, then excludable employees, then benefiting employees, separately for deferral, match and any nonelective component.
Run the ratio percentage test - the percentage of non-highly compensated employees benefiting divided by the percentage of highly compensated employees benefiting, tested against 70 percent.
Where the ratio percentage fails, run the average benefit test with its nondiscriminatory classification and average benefit percentage components and record both results.
Record the exact populations and counts used so the result can be reproduced from the census.
Escalate a coverage failure immediately - the correction is bringing employees into the plan, which takes longer than a refund.
checklist.done: coverage is tested by component with the ratio percentage computed and the average benefit test run and documented where needed.

checklist.step: Run the ADP and ACP tests
actions: Compute each eligible employee's actual deferral percentage as deferrals divided by plan compensation, including eligible employees who deferred zero.
Compute the HCE and NHCE group averages and apply the basic test and the alternative 2 times and 2 percentage point test.
Record the prior year or current year testing method the plan document elects and use it - switching methods without an amendment is not available.
Run the ACP test on matching and after-tax contributions on the same basis, and confirm catch-up contributions are excluded from ADP where properly recharacterised.
Produce the result pack showing populations, averages, the test applied and the pass or fail margin, and sign it with the run date and parameters.
checklist.done: signed ADP and ACP result packs show group averages, the elected testing method and the pass or fail margin, reproducible from the census.

checklist.step: Run the 401(a)(4) general test where required
actions: Determine whether any allocation formula falls outside a design-based safe harbour - for example an integrated, cross-tested or new comparability allocation.
Run the general test on allocation rates or, where cross-testing, on equivalent benefit accrual rates using the permitted testing age and interest assumptions, and record the assumptions.
Test any benefits, rights and features available to some but not all participants for current and effective availability.
Where restructuring or rate grouping is used to pass, document each group's composition and the reason it is a permissible grouping.
Sign the result with the method, assumptions and populations used.
checklist.done: the general test is run with recorded assumptions and groupings, and benefits, rights and features availability is tested and documented.

checklist.step: Run the top-heavy determination
actions: Value key employee and total account balances as at the determination date - the last day of the preceding plan year - and compute the key employee ratio against the 60 percent threshold.
Include the required rollovers and distributions in the look-back period and exclude unrelated rollovers, showing each adjustment.
Aggregate required and permissively aggregated plans and state which plans are in the aggregation group.
Where the plan is top-heavy, compute the minimum contribution owed to each non-key participant employed on the last day and hand the funding schedule to the Controller.
Sign the determination with the valuation date, balances and the resulting ratio.
checklist.done: a signed top-heavy determination shows the key employee ratio against 60 percent, the aggregation group and any minimum contribution schedule.

checklist.step: Run the 415(c) annual additions test
actions: Sum each participant's annual additions for the limitation year: elective deferrals excluding catch-up, employer match, nonelective contributions and forfeiture allocations.
Test each against the lesser of the dollar limit for the limitation year and 100 percent of IRC 415(c)(3) compensation.
Aggregate additions across all defined contribution plans of the controlled group, since the limit is per employee and not per plan.
List every excess with the participant id, the amount and the component that caused it, and hand it to the correction owner.
Record the limitation year definition used from the plan document.
checklist.done: annual additions are computed per participant across all plans in the group and tested against the 415(c) limit, with excesses listed.

checklist.step: Write the prudence record behind every judgement
actions: For each election made - prior versus current year ADP method, top-paid group, permissive aggregation, disaggregation of otherwise excludable employees - record the plan document authority, the alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was appropriate.
Record who made each judgement, on what data and on what date, so the process is defensible independently of whether the answer was right.
Where an election changes a failing result into a passing one, escalate it to Employment Counsel for review before it is relied on.
Attach the prudence record to the testing workpaper as the ERISA 404(a)(1)(B) evidence.
checklist.done: every testing election and judgement has a dated record naming the authority, alternatives, decider and data used.

checklist.step: Decide the correction method and execute inside 2.5 months
actions: For an ADP or ACP failure choose between corrective distribution to HCEs using the leveling method, a qualified nonelective contribution to NHCEs, or a combination, and document the cost and participant impact of each.
Compute the excess contributions by dollar leveling, allocate them to HCEs in order of contribution amount and compute allocable earnings to the distribution date.
Execute the correction by 15 March for a calendar plan year to avoid the 10 percent employer excise tax on excess amounts, and in all cases within 12 months of plan year end to protect qualification.
Where the deadline for excise-free correction is already missed, prepare Form 5330 with the Tax Manager and pay the excise tax rather than delay the correction further.
Have Employment Counsel approve the chosen method and record the approval date.
checklist.done: a counsel-approved correction is computed with earnings and executed by 15 March, or by the 12-month date with Form 5330 filed.

checklist.step: Process the refunds, contributions and tax reporting
actions: Send the corrective distribution file to the recordkeeper with participant id, gross amount, earnings and the distribution reason code.
Confirm the 1099-R coding is correct for the distribution type and year of taxation, and that 402(g) excess deferrals distributed by 15 April are reported for the correct year.
Fund any QNEC or top-heavy minimum from the employer account by the deadline and obtain the trust deposit confirmation.
Reconcile the amounts actually distributed and funded back to the correction calculation to the dollar.
Notify affected participants with an explanation letter approved by Employment Counsel.
checklist.done: distributions and contributions are executed, tied back to the calculation, correctly coded on 1099-R and explained to affected participants.

checklist.step: Report the testing results to the plan committee
actions: Present the result pack: each test, the margin by which it passed or failed, the corrections made and their cost, and the root cause of any failure.
Present the forward actions - plan design change, safe harbour adoption, automatic enrolment or targeted NHCE communication - with owners and dates.
Record the committee decision and the minute reference against the plan year testing file.
Escalate any failure that reached the 12-month backstop to the Audit Committee as a qualification risk.
checklist.done: results, corrections, root causes and forward actions are presented and minuted, with 12-month failures escalated to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Retain the testing workpapers
actions: File the signed census and validation results, the payroll reconciliation, the HCE and key employee determinations, the scope memo, every test result pack with its parameters, the prudence record and the correction calculations with funding proof.
Apply a 6-year ERISA 107 retention label to the supporting records and an indefinite label to the qualification support, which an IRS examination can reach back to.
Index by plan number, plan year and test type so a single test can be produced on request.
Run a completeness check that every required test for every plan has a filed result pack.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed testing file exists per plan and plan year with qualification support retained indefinitely.

testing.step: Build the population of plans, tests and corrections
actions: List every plan in the controlled group requiring testing for the plan year and the tests each requires, taken from the plan documents and the scope memo.
Extract every test result pack filed for the year and every corrective distribution, forfeiture reallocation and QNEC from the recordkeeping transaction history.
Extract the signed census with its record count and the payroll control totals for the same period.
Record the population counts, extraction method and timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: required tests, filed results and executed corrections are populated per plan with counts and extraction method recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the census to payroll and the recordkeeper
actions: Reconcile census headcount to the payroll active and terminated employee counts for the plan year and investigate every difference.
Reconcile total census compensation to the payroll general ledger control total and total deferrals to the trust remittance file.
Confirm eligible non-deferrers and mid-year terminees are present in the census - sample 20 terminees from payroll and confirm each appears.
Confirm every required test in the scope memo has a filed result pack and list any test not run.
testing.done: census counts and compensation reconcile to payroll and the trust, non-deferrers and terminees are proven present, and unrun tests are listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of failed tests, 100% of corrections and 100% of plans that changed testing method or election this year.
Take 40 census records at random using a recorded seed, stratified to include 15 HCEs and 10 terminees.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
State which test and which assertion each sampled item supports.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample covering all failures, corrections and election changes is drawn with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the HCE and key employee determination
actions: For each sampled record take the lookback year compensation from payroll and the ownership data from the legal entity records and reach your own HCE conclusion.
Re-apply IRC 318 family attribution independently and compare the attribution chains to those recorded.
Where the top-paid group election was used, re-rank the population and confirm the same 20 percent cut-off was applied.
Record any misclassified HCE as a fail and quantify its effect on the ADP and ACP results.
testing.done: HCE and key employee status is independently re-determined for every sampled record with attribution re-applied and misclassifications quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the coverage, ADP and ACP results
actions: Rebuild the ADP calculation from the census in an independent workbook: deferral percentage per eligible employee, group averages, and both the basic and the 2 times 2 tests.
Rebuild the ACP calculation on match and after-tax contributions on the same basis and confirm catch-up recharacterisation was applied correctly.
Rebuild the 410(b) ratio percentage from the benefiting and excludable populations and compare to the filed result.
Compare your results to the filed packs and treat any difference in the pass or fail conclusion, or in the excess amount, as an exception - including a right answer reached from a wrong population.
testing.done: ADP, ACP and coverage are independently rebuilt from the census and reconciled to the filed results, with any difference recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the top-heavy and 415(c) limit tests
actions: Recompute the top-heavy ratio from account balances at the determination date, re-applying the distribution look-back and rollover adjustments.
Confirm the aggregation group used matches the scope memo and the plan documents.
Recompute annual additions for the sampled participants across every defined contribution plan in the controlled group and compare to the 415(c) limit for the limitation year.
Recompute 402(g) deferrals for the sampled participants and confirm any excess was distributed with earnings by 15 April.
testing.done: top-heavy, 415(c) and 402(g) results are independently recomputed with aggregation scope confirmed and excess distributions verified.

testing.step: Recompute the correction amounts and their deadline maths
actions: Recompute the excess contribution by dollar leveling and the HCE allocation order, then recompute allocable earnings to the actual distribution date.
Compare your figures to the amounts actually distributed or funded from the recordkeeping transaction history, participant by participant.
Recompute the 2.5-month excise-free date and the 12-month qualification date from the plan year end and compare both to the execution date.
Where the 2.5-month date was missed, confirm Form 5330 was filed and the 10 percent excise tax paid on the correct base.
testing.done: correction amounts and earnings are recomputed participant by participant and both statutory dates are recomputed against the actual execution date.

testing.step: Test the prudence record behind the elections
actions: For each sampled election open the prudence record and confirm it names the plan document authority, the alternatives considered, the decider and the date.
Confirm the elected ADP method matches the plan document and that no method changed without an amendment.
For any election that turned a failing result into a passing one, confirm the counsel review pre-dates reliance on it.
Record an election with no contemporaneous reasoning as a prudence failure under ERISA 404(a)(1)(B), even where the numerical answer was correct.
testing.done: each sampled election is supported by a contemporaneous, dated prudence record with counsel review where the result turned on it.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan number, plan year, test, participants affected and the dollar impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (census incomplete, compensation definition misapplied, HCE misclassified, election unsupported, correction late, limit not aggregated) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and open an EPCRS assessment with Employment Counsel where an operational failure occurred, covering self-correction eligibility or a VCP submission.
Carry every open issue into the next year's July interim run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, owner, dollar impact and an EPCRS assessment where an operational failure occurred.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the proportion of required tests run and independently reproduced, and the count of corrections executed after the 2.5-month date.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing plan numbers, test names and workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer - who produced no census, ran no test and calculated no correction for the year - sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any qualification risk to the Plan Investment & Administration Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with reproduction statistics, a stated conclusion and committee reporting dates is filed in the evidence repository.
